## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

--- PYPROJECT ---
[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[project]
name = "researchgpt"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "A Multi-Agent Agentic RAG Platform for Automated Literature Review"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
license = { text = "MIT" }
authors = [
    { name = "Abrarullah Mohammed" },
    { name = "G. Shashivadan Rao" },
    { name = "P. Sreekaran Reddy" },
]

# Runtime deps are grouped so a partial install still gets you a working CLI.
# Verified to resolve on Python 3.14.6 (2026-08-25).
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.7",
    "pyyaml>=6.0",
    "typer>=0.12",
    "httpx>=0.27",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
# Phase 2 — retrieval. Heavy (pulls torch); install when Phase 2 starts.
retrieval = [
    "chromadb>=1.0",
    "rank-bm25>=0.2.2",
    "sentence-transformers>=3.0",
    "pymupdf>=1.24",
]
# Phase 4/5 — the agent graph.
graph = [
    "langgraph>=0.2",
    "langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite>=1.0",
]
# Phase 5 — verifier inference on CPU. No torch needed at run time.
verify = [
    "onnxruntime>=1.18",
    "transformers>=4.40",
    # DeBERTa-v3 uses a SentencePiece tokenizer. Without these two the
    # tokenizer fails to load with a misleading "conversion" error - verified
    # missing on this machine 2026-08-25. Kaggle ships them; local does not.
    "sentencepiece>=0.2",
    "protobuf>=4.25",
    "optimum[onnxruntime]>=1.20",   # ONNX export + int8 quantization (T-304)
]
# Phase 6 — API layer.
api = [
    "fastapi>=0.110",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.29",
    "sse-starlette>=2.0",
]
# Phase 3B — SciReviewGen parsing.
scireviewgen = [
    "datasets>=2.19",
    "pyarrow>=16.0",
]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23",
    "ruff>=0.4",
]

[project.scripts]
researchgpt = "researchgpt.cli:app"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/researchgpt"]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
target-version = "py311"

[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
pythonpath = ["src"]

# ResearchGPT — Master Task List

> **What this file is.** The single executable backlog for the whole project, derived from `PROJECT_PLAN.md`, `RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md`, `SESSION_CONTEXT.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md` and the two `diagrams/*_EXPLAINED.md` files.
>
> **Two-agent workflow.** **Claude Code plans, specifies, reviews and integrates. Cursor (Groq) writes the code.** Every task below is written so it can be handed to Cursor as a self-contained unit of work with a hard acceptance test.
>
> **Companion documents:** `TRAINING_SPEC.md` (both fine-tuned models — verifier and reranker — and why the generative agents are not trained), `DB_SCHEMA.md` (the Postgres run registry), `PROJECT_PLAN.md` (scope), `SESSION_CONTEXT.md` (constraints and literature findings).
>
> Created 2026-08-25. Update the checkboxes in place; do not rewrite the file.

---

## 0. Reality check — read this before anything else

| | |
|---|---|
| Plan written | 2026-08-06 (30-day plan, Day 1 = 2026-08-07) |
| Today | **2026-08-25** |
| Target submission | **~2026-09-07** (was ~09-05; +2 days authorised 2026-08-25 to integrate SciReviewGen) |
| Days actually remaining | **13** |
| Code written so far | **Zero.** No `src/`, no `pyproject.toml`, no `.py` file anywhere in the folder. |

**The 30-day plan is no longer executable as written.** Nineteen of its thirty days are gone and none of them produced code. What exists is planning, literature, design and two graded decks.

This file is therefore **not** the 30-day plan re-typed. It is a compressed 11-day plan that applies the descope ladder in `PROJECT_PLAN.md §10` **up front** rather than in a panic on Day 28. Concretely, the following are cut before starting, not deferred:

| Cut now | Was | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Ollama feasibility probe | §6.3 | Already demoted to a footnote. Dead. |
| DOCX writer | §2.2 | Markdown + PDF-from-Markdown suffices. |
| 2-annotator Likert + Cohen's κ | §9 | Scheduling cost exceeds its evidentiary value at 11 days. Replaced by the 50-claim spot-check. |
| Ablations 3 and 4 | §9.4 | Kept only if Phase 7 finishes early. **Ablation 2 is never cut.** |
| Extraction F1 annotation (10 papers) | §5.4 | Replaced by 5 qualitative examples. |

**Reinstated 2026-08-25: SciReviewGen is back in scope (Phase 3B).** The original cut rested on a premise that turned out to be false — `PROJECT_PLAN.md §5.3` assumed distribution "as preprocessing scripts over S2ORC, historically requiring an AI2 access request with days of latency." **Three ungated public mirrors exist on Hugging Face** (`kejian/SciReviewGen`, `kdercksen/scireviewgen-csv`, `pat-jj/SciReviewGen`), verified downloadable 2026-08-25. There is no access request and no lead time. Two days were authorised for the integration; the schedule absorbs them at the back (§13).

**Never cut, under any circumstance** — these seven are the project: the six agents, the trained **verifier** (the reranker fine-tune in Phase 3C is a *second* trained model and is explicitly droppable — see T-335), the evidence-inspection panel, ablation 2 (− Verifier), `trace.jsonl`, the **M1 milestone** (first complete cited survey), the **SciReviewGen verifier cross-check (T-325)**, and — as of the 2026-08-25 decision — **Human-in-the-Loop (T-609)**.

> If M1 has not landed by **2026-08-31**, stop building forward and stabilise what exists. A working four-agent pipeline that produces a cited survey beats a half-wired six-agent graph that runs nothing.

---

## 0.1 Model policy — HARD RULE, no exceptions ★

**Only free, open-weight models. No paid models, no paid tiers, no trial credits, at any point in this project.**

This is Constraint 1 from `SESSION_CONTEXT.md §2` and it is not negotiable. If a task cannot be done on the allowlist below, the task gets descoped — the budget does not get raised.

### Allowlist — verified live on 2026-08-25

Every generative agent (Planner, Extractor, Critic, Writer) runs on one of these. All are **open-weight** models on a **free tier**, so the project is $0 by construction rather than by discipline.

| Model | Provider | Weights | Verified | Use for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gemma-4-31b-it` | Google AI Studio | open | ✅ HTTP 200, extracted correctly | **Primary candidate** — all four agents |
| `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` | Google AI Studio | open (MoE, ~4B active) | ⚠️ HTTP 200 but returned `{}` on the extraction probe | Speed fallback only; re-test before use |
| `openai/gpt-oss-120b` | Groq | open (Apache 2.0) | ✅ HTTP 200 | **Primary backup** — largest free open-weight option |
| `openai/gpt-oss-20b` | Groq | open (Apache 2.0) | not yet probed | Lightweight fallback |
| `qwen/qwen3.6-27b` | Groq | open | ✅ HTTP 200 | Second backup / bake-off arm |

*Despite the name, `openai/gpt-oss-*` are OpenAI's **open-weight** releases served free by Groq. They are not the paid OpenAI API.*

### Forbidden — do not call, do not put in a config, do not benchmark against

`gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gpt-4*`, `o1/o3/o4`, Claude API models, `gemini-*-pro`, `deep-research-*`, and every other metered endpoint. **`RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §10.1` still names `gpt-4o-mini` and `gpt-4o` in `configs/default.yaml` — that config is from before the $0 constraint existed and must not be copied verbatim (see T-106).**

Proprietary free-tier models (`gemini-3.6-flash` and friends) are $0 today, but they are **not open-weight**, so a tier change can strand the project mid-build. They are permitted only as a temporary unblock, must be logged in the trace when used, and must never be the model reported in the paper.

### Enforcement, not good intentions

- **T-104 (`core/llm.py`) hard-fails on any model outside the allowlist.** The list lives in one constant in that file. A model not in it raises before any HTTP request is made. This is the whole enforcement mechanism — see T-104's acceptance criterion.
- The allowlist constant is the single source of truth. `configs/default.yaml` may only name models that appear in it.
- Every `trace.jsonl` LLM event records the model name, so the paper's "which model produced this" question is answerable from the run log.

### Measured consequence — Gemma ignores `responseSchema`

Probed 2026-08-25: Gemma on the Gemini API accepts `generationConfig.responseSchema` but **does not honour it**. It returns markdown-fenced JSON (a leading space and a trailing ```` ``` ````), not native structured output, and `gemma-4-26b-a4b-it` ignored the content entirely and returned `{}`.

This is not a blocker — it is a known cost of the $0 rule, and the plan already budgets for it (`SPEC §14`, retry-with-repair max 2). It has two consequences:

Source of truth: RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §8. Every other module imports its shapes
from here; nothing in this file may import from the rest of the package, so it
stays dependency-free and safe to import anywhere.

Deviations from SPEC §8, all deliberate and recorded in TASKLIST.md:

* ``Paper.text_availability`` is new. TASKLIST T-204 sets it and T-505 enforces
  the abstract-only rule that depends on it (abstract-only papers may be cited
  as existing but may not supply verified claims).
* ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` lives here rather than in ``core/llm.py`` as TASKLIST §0.1
  originally said. Reason: this module has no dependencies, so ``core/config.py``
  can validate model names at config-load time instead of failing at the first
  API call. ``core/llm.py`` still owns *enforcement* — it imports and checks this
  constant before constructing any request.
* ``RunConfig`` and its nested models are new. SPEC §10.1 specifies the YAML but
  never types it, and SPEC's version predates the $0 constraint.
"""

from typing import Literal, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

# Enumerations (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

    "scopus_q1", "scopus", "ieee", "acl", "peer_reviewed", "preprint", "unknown"
]
Verdict = Literal["SUPPORTED", "PARTIAL", "UNSUPPORTED", "CONTRADICTED"]
Decision = Literal["WRITE", "RETRIEVE", "REPLAN"]
TextAvailability = Literal["full", "abstract_only", "none"]

#: TASKLIST §0.1 — the $0 hard rule. Only free, open-weight models.

        # Google AI Studio — open-weight Gemma, free tier
        "gemma-4-31b-it",
        "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
        # Groq — open-weight, free tier
        "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
        "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
        "qwen/qwen3.6-27b",
    }
)

#: Provider inferred from model name; used by ``core/llm.py`` to pick a client.
MODEL_PROVIDER: dict[str, str] = {
    "gemma-4-31b-it": "google",
    "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it": "google",
    "openai/gpt-oss-120b": "groq",
    "openai/gpt-oss-20b": "groq",
    "qwen/qwen3.6-27b": "groq",
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corpus models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Paper(BaseModel):
    paper_id: str
    doi: Optional[str] = None
    title: str
    authors: list[str] = []
    year: Optional[int] = None
    venue: Optional[str] = None
    venue_tier: VenueTier = "unknown"
    abstract: Optional[str] = None
    url: Optional[str] = None
    pdf_path: Optional[str] = None
    source: str  # openalex | arxiv
    citation_count: Optional[int] = None

    #: Set by the PDF loader (T-204). Gates claim sourcing under T-505.
    text_availability: TextAvailability = "none"


class Chunk(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    paper_id: str
    text: str
    section: Optional[str] = None  # abstract | methods | results | ...
    start_char: int
    end_char: int
    embedding_id: Optional[str] = None

    @field_validator("end_char")
    @classmethod
    def _end_after_start(cls, v: int, info) -> int:
        start = info.data.get("start_char")
        if start is not None and v < start:
            raise ValueError(f"end_char {v} precedes start_char {start}")
        return v


class EvidenceSpan(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    quote: str
    start_char: int
    end_char: int


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent output models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class PaperInsight(BaseModel):
    """Extractor output. The four graded fields are all Optional by design:
    SPEC §14.2 forbids fabrication, so an unresolvable field is ``None`` plus an
    ``extraction_note``, never an invented string."""

    paper_id: str

"""LangGraph state definition.

Source of truth: RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §8.1.

The reducer choice on each field is the load-bearing part of this file, because
the Critic loop (TASKLIST T-507) can re-enter ``retriever`` and ``planner`` up to
three times. Getting a reducer wrong shows up as silently duplicated papers or
silently lost insights on iteration 2, which is expensive to debug once six
agents sit on top of it.

The rule applied here:

* **Accumulate** (``add``) anything the loop legitimately gathers more of across
  iterations: papers, chunks, log lines.
* **Replace** (default) anything an agent recomputes wholesale each pass:
  insights, claims, the draft, the Critic's decision.

``papers`` and ``chunks`` accumulate, so the retriever must deduplicate by
``paper_id`` / ``chunk_id`` before returning — the reducer will not do it.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from operator import add
from typing import Annotated, Any, TypedDict

from researchgpt.core.models import (
    Chunk,
    Claim,
    Paper,
    PaperInsight,
    SearchTask,
    SubQuestion,
)


def _merge_dict(left: dict, right: dict) -> dict:
    """Shallow-merge reducer for dict fields written by more than one node."""
    return {**left, **right}


class ReviewState(TypedDict, total=False):
    # ---- input -----------------------------------------------------------
    run_id: str
    research_question: str
    constraints: dict  # years, venues, max_papers, language

    # ---- planner ---------------------------------------------------------
    # Replaced wholesale on REPLAN: a replan supersedes the previous plan
    # rather than adding to it (SPEC §7.5 requires a plan diff on replan).
    sub_questions: list[SubQuestion]
    search_plan: list[SearchTask]
    inclusion_criteria: list[str]

    # ---- retriever -------------------------------------------------------
    # Accumulated: a RETRIEVE loop is meant to add coverage, not start over.
    # Retriever MUST dedupe by paper_id / chunk_id before returning.
    papers: Annotated[list[Paper], add]
    chunks: Annotated[list[Chunk], add]
    retrieval_log: Annotated[list[dict], add]

    # ---- extractor / verifier -------------------------------------------
    # Replaced: recomputed over the full corpus each pass.
    paper_insights: list[PaperInsight]
    verified_claims: list[Claim]
    #: Dropped claims. Surfaced in Vue panel 4 (T-608) and counted in the
    #: trace — TASKLIST calls this "the real measure of what the architecture
    #: buys", so it is state, not a side effect.
    unsupported_claims: list[Claim]
    contradiction_pairs: list[tuple[str, str]]
    grounding_score: float

    # ---- critic ----------------------------------------------------------
    decision: str  # WRITE | RETRIEVE | REPLAN
    critic_feedback: str
    coverage_report: dict
    #: Hard-capped at review.max_iterations by routing.py (T-507).
    iteration: int
    #: Append-only audit of every routing decision, so an oscillating loop is
    #: diagnosable after the fact rather than by re-running.
    decision_log: Annotated[list[dict], add]

    # ---- human in the loop (T-609, gated on the T-007 decision) ----------
    human_overrides: Annotated[list[dict], add]

    # ---- writer ----------------------------------------------------------
    themes: list[dict]
    draft_sections: dict
    final_review: str
    artefacts: Annotated[dict[str, Any], _merge_dict]


#: Fields the Planner is allowed to overwrite on a REPLAN. Used by routing.py
#: to compute the mandatory plan diff (SPEC §7.5).
PLAN_FIELDS = ("sub_questions", "search_plan", "inclusion_criteria")

__all__ = ["ReviewState", "PLAN_FIELDS"]

"""ResearchGPT CLI entry point.

``run`` currently wires config + TraceLogger only; later phases fill in the
pipeline. Declared as the ``researchgpt`` console script in pyproject.toml.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from importlib.metadata import PackageNotFoundError, version as pkg_version

import typer

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.core.logging import TraceLogger

app = typer.Typer(add_completion=False)


@app.command()
def version() -> None:
    try:
        ver = pkg_version("researchgpt")
    except PackageNotFoundError:
        ver = "0.0.0-dev"
    typer.echo(ver)


@app.command()
def run(
    question: str = typer.Option(..., "--question", "-q"),
    max_papers: int = typer.Option(None, "--max-papers"),
    config: str = typer.Option("configs/default.yaml", "--config"),
    fixture: bool = typer.Option(False, "--fixture"),
) -> None:
    run_id = f"{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
    overrides: dict | None = None
    if max_papers is not None:
        overrides = {"review": {"max_papers": max_papers}}
    cfg = load_config(config, overrides=overrides)

    with TraceLogger(run_id, runs_dir=cfg.output.runs_dir) as trace:
        trace.event(
            agent="cli",
            event="run_start",
            payload={
                "question": question,
                "fixture": fixture,
                "config": cfg.model_dump(),
            },
        )
        typer.echo(f"run_id={run_id}")
        typer.echo(f"run_dir={trace.run_dir}")
        trace.event(agent="cli", event="run_end", payload={"ok": True})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

# ResearchGPT — default run configuration
#
# Typed by src/researchgpt/core/models.py::RunConfig. Unknown keys are rejected.
#
# NOTE: this file deliberately does NOT follow RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §10.1's
# `llm:` block. That block names gpt-4o-mini and gpt-4o, which are forbidden
# under TASKLIST §0.1 ($0, free open-weight models only). The spec's config
# predates the zero-budget constraint.
#
# T-004 BAKE-OFF: COMPLETE (2026-08-25). 5 real gold-set abstracts per arm,
# through the real extractor_v1 prompt and the real LLMClient.
#
#   arm                   parse valid fields echo   avg lat   verdict
#   openai/gpt-oss-120b    100%  100%  4.6/8    0     26.6s   PRIMARY
#   qwen/qwen3.6-27b       100%  100%  7.0/8  2/5     41.8s   rejected
#   gemma-4-31b-it            -     -      -    -         -   disqualified
#   gemma-4-26b-a4b-it        -     -      -    -         -   disqualified
#
# WHY gpt-oss WINS DESPITE LOWER FIELD COVERAGE:
#   qwen echoed the literal schema placeholder "string" into datasets/metrics
#   on 2 of 5 papers (40%). That is the worst possible failure mode here: it
#   parses, it validates, and it silently injects fabricated content into a
#   hallucination-graded pipeline (SPEC §14.2 forbids exactly this).
#   qwen's 7.0/8 field score is itself INFLATED by the echo - excluding the
#   echoed rows it scores 6.33/8. gpt-oss echoed 0/5.
#
# KNOWN WEAKNESS OF THE WINNER: gpt-oss populates only 4.6/8 content fields.
#   This is most likely a PROMPT problem, not a model problem - extractor_v1
#   ships 3 few-shot examples and Dagdelen et al. measured structured output
#   stabilising at ~20. T-404 must expand the few-shots, then re-run this
#   bake-off and expect the field count to rise.
#
# LATENCY REALITY CHECK (TASKLIST §0.2 tolerance is ~30 min/run):
#   gpt-oss ~26.6s/paper x ~70 papers = ~31 min for the extraction stage
#   alone. Right at the tolerance. The response cache makes re-runs free, but
#   the FIRST full run will sit near 30-40 min end to end.
#   Groq latency is highly variable under load (measured 3.8s-55s same arm).

llm:
  model: openai/gpt-oss-120b       # Extractor / Critic / Writer — 27x faster
  planner_model: openai/gpt-oss-120b   # Planner
  temperature: 0.1
  max_tokens: 4096
  requests_per_minute: 15          # free-tier throttle (T-104)
  max_retries: 5
  cache_dir: data/llm_cache        # prompt-hash cache (T-104)

embeddings:
  model: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5    # CPU-sized, down from bge-large
  device: cpu
  batch_size: 32

retrieval:
  dense_k: 30
  sparse_k: 30
  fusion: rrf
  rrf_k: 60
  rerank: true
  reranker: cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2   # ~22M, CPU
  final_k: 12
  chunk_size: 1200
  chunk_overlap: 200

sources:
  # OpenAlex is the mandatory primary (reliable, keyless, rich venue/OA data).
  # Semantic Scholar reinstated 2026-08-25 (TASKLIST §0.2): claimed on 8 slides
  # of the Review-2 deck, and its rate limiting is survivable now that latency
  # is not a constraint. It is BEST-EFFORT — on sustained 429s the run
  # continues on openalex + arxiv. Crossref stays cut (redundant).
  enabled: [openalex, arxiv, semantic_scholar]
  max_per_source: 25

review:
  min_papers: 20
  max_papers: 60                   # 25 for ablation runs
  year_min: 2019
  max_iterations: 3                # hard cap, forced WRITE on the last
  grounding_threshold: 0.7
  coverage_threshold: 0.8

verifier:
  onnx_path: data/models/verifier-int8.onnx
  tokenizer: microsoft/deberta-v3-small
  support_threshold: 0.7           # biased to precision (T-503)

output:
  citation_style: ieee
  formats: [markdown, csv, bibtex]
  runs_dir: outputs/runs

    config: str = typer.Option("configs/default.yaml", "--config"),
    fixture: bool = typer.Option(False, "--fixture"),
) -> None:
    run_id = f"{datetime.now(timezone.utc):%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}"
    overrides: dict | None = None
    if max_papers is not None:
        overrides = {"review": {"max_papers": max_papers}}
    cfg = load_config(config, overrides=overrides)

    with TraceLogger(run_id, runs_dir=cfg.output.runs_dir) as trace:
        trace.event(
            agent="cli",
            event="run_start",
            payload={
                "question": question,
                "fixture": fixture,
                "config": cfg.model_dump(),
            },
        )
        typer.echo(f"run_id={run_id}")
        typer.echo(f"run_dir={trace.run_dir}")
        trace.event(agent="cli", event="run_end", payload={"ok": True})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    app()

"""T-212 — retrieval recall against the project's own bibliography.

Measures whether the corpus builder finds the papers a human curator found.

**Gate note.** `PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.2` specifies "Recall@20 >= 0.80". With a
35-paper gold set that is unachievable: retrieving 20 papers caps recall at
20/35 = 0.57. The corrected gate (TASKLIST T-212) is **Recall@60 >= 0.80**,
where 60 is ``review.max_papers`` - the corpus the Extractor actually sees and
therefore the thing downstream quality depends on. Recall@20 is still reported
as a secondary diagnostic, labelled with its ceiling.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import search_arxiv, search_openalex

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")

#: Stands in for the Planner (T-402), which does not exist yet. These mirror
#: the six thematic clusters of the literature review (SPEC §1.6) so the
#: evaluation reflects the real multi-sub-question retrieval pattern rather
#: than a single lucky query.
QUERIES = [
    # SHORT queries — 2-4 terms. OpenAlex ANDs every term in
    # title_and_abstract.search, so a 6-term query matches almost nothing
    # (measured 2026-08-25: "scientific claim verification evidence entailment
    # SciFact" -> 0 results; "scientific claim verification" -> 4,174).
    # This constraint must be reflected in the Planner prompt (T-402).
    "agentic retrieval augmented generation",
    "automated literature review generation",
    "scientific survey generation",
    "scientific claim verification",
    "citation accuracy language models",
    "hallucination large language models",
    "retrieval augmented generation evaluation",
    "multi-agent large language model",
    "systematic review automation",
    "cross-encoder reranking retrieval",
    "attributed question answering citations",
    "scientific information extraction",
    "citation text generation",
    "evidence retrieval fact checking",
    "RAG survey",
]


def norm(doi: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not doi:
        return None
    return doi.strip().lower().replace("https://doi.org/", "")


def main() -> None:
    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    gold = {norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    print(f"gold set: {len(gold)} DOIs\n", flush=True)

    per_query: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    union: dict[str, Any] = {}          # doi -> first rank seen
    ordered: list[str] = []             # dedup order across queries

    for q in QUERIES:
        found: list[str] = []
        try:
            papers = search_openalex(q, year_min=cfg.review.year_min, max_results=25)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  openalex failed on {q[:40]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)
            papers = []
        try:
            papers += search_arxiv(q, max_results=15)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  arxiv failed on {q[:40]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)

        for p in papers:
            d = norm(p.doi)
            if not d:
                continue
            if d not in union:
                union[d] = len(ordered)
                ordered.append(d)
            if d in gold:
                found.append(d)

        hit = len(set(found))
        per_query.append({"query": q, "retrieved": len(papers), "gold_hits": hit})
        print(f"  {hit:2d} gold hits / {len(papers):3d} retrieved  |  {q[:52]}", flush=True)

    # Recall at increasing corpus cut-offs.
    recalls = {}
    for k in (20, 40, 60, 100, len(ordered)):
        if k <= 0:
            continue
        top = set(ordered[:k])
        recalls[k] = len(top & gold) / len(gold)

    found_all = set(ordered) & gold
    missed = sorted(gold - found_all)

    print(f"\nunion corpus: {len(ordered)} unique DOIs across {len(QUERIES)} queries", flush=True)
    print("\nRECALL")
    for k, v in recalls.items():
        ceiling = min(k, len(gold)) / len(gold)
        label = "  <- GATE (max_papers)" if k == 60 else ""
        note = f"  [ceiling {ceiling:.2f}]" if ceiling < 1.0 else ""
        print(f"  Recall@{k:<5d} = {v:.3f}{note}{label}", flush=True)

    gate = recalls.get(60, 0.0)
    print(f"\nGATE  Recall@60 >= 0.80  ->  {gate:.3f}  {'PASS' if gate >= 0.80 else 'FAIL'}")

"""T-212 — retrieval recall against the project's own bibliography.

Measures whether the corpus builder finds the papers a human curator found.

**Gate note.** `PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.2` specifies "Recall@20 >= 0.80". With a
35-paper gold set that is unachievable: retrieving 20 papers caps recall at
20/35 = 0.57. The corrected gate (TASKLIST T-212) is **Recall@60 >= 0.80**,
where 60 is ``review.max_papers`` - the corpus the Extractor actually sees and
therefore the thing downstream quality depends on. Recall@20 is still reported
as a secondary diagnostic, labelled with its ceiling.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import search_arxiv, search_openalex

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")

#: Stands in for the Planner (T-402), which does not exist yet. These mirror
#: the six thematic clusters of the literature review (SPEC §1.6) so the
#: evaluation reflects the real multi-sub-question retrieval pattern rather
#: than a single lucky query.
QUERIES = [
    # SHORT queries — 2-4 terms. OpenAlex ANDs every term in
    # title_and_abstract.search, so a 6-term query matches almost nothing
    # (measured 2026-08-25: "scientific claim verification evidence entailment
    # SciFact" -> 0 results; "scientific claim verification" -> 4,174).
    # This constraint must be reflected in the Planner prompt (T-402).
    "agentic retrieval augmented generation",
    "automated literature review generation",
    "scientific survey generation",
    "scientific claim verification",
    "citation accuracy language models",
    "hallucination large language models",
    "retrieval augmented generation evaluation",
    "multi-agent large language model",
    "systematic review automation",
    "cross-encoder reranking retrieval",
    "attributed question answering citations",
    "scientific information extraction",
    "citation text generation",
    "evidence retrieval fact checking",
    "RAG survey",
]


def norm(doi: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not doi:
        return None
    return doi.strip().lower().replace("https://doi.org/", "")


def main() -> None:
    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    gold = {norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    print(f"gold set: {len(gold)} DOIs\n", flush=True)

    per_query: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    union: dict[str, Any] = {}          # doi -> first rank seen
    ordered: list[str] = []             # dedup order across queries

    for q in QUERIES:
        found: list[str] = []
        try:
            papers = search_openalex(q, year_min=cfg.review.year_min, max_results=25)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  openalex failed on {q[:40]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)
            papers = []
        try:
            papers += search_arxiv(q, max_results=15)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  arxiv failed on {q[:40]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)

        for p in papers:
            d = norm(p.doi)
            if not d:
                continue
            if d not in union:
                union[d] = len(ordered)
                ordered.append(d)
            if d in gold:
                found.append(d)

        hit = len(set(found))
        per_query.append({"query": q, "retrieved": len(papers), "gold_hits": hit})
        print(f"  {hit:2d} gold hits / {len(papers):3d} retrieved  |  {q[:52]}", flush=True)

    # Recall at increasing corpus cut-offs.
    recalls = {}
    for k in (20, 40, 60, 100, len(ordered)):
        if k <= 0:
            continue
        top = set(ordered[:k])
        recalls[k] = len(top & gold) / len(gold)

    found_all = set(ordered) & gold
    missed = sorted(gold - found_all)

    print(f"\nunion corpus: {len(ordered)} unique DOIs across {len(QUERIES)} queries", flush=True)
    print("\nRECALL")
    for k, v in recalls.items():
        ceiling = min(k, len(gold)) / len(gold)
        label = "  <- GATE (max_papers)" if k == 60 else ""
        note = f"  [ceiling {ceiling:.2f}]" if ceiling < 1.0 else ""
        print(f"  Recall@{k:<5d} = {v:.3f}{note}{label}", flush=True)

    gate = recalls.get(60, 0.0)
    print(f"\nGATE  Recall@60 >= 0.80  ->  {gate:.3f}  {'PASS' if gate >= 0.80 else 'FAIL'}")
    print(f"found {len(found_all)}/{len(gold)} gold papers; missed {len(missed)}")
    if missed:
        by_doi = {norm(p["doi"]): p for p in gold_doc["papers"]}
        print("\nMISSED (these bound every downstream metric):")
        for d in missed[:15]:
            p = by_doi.get(d, {})
            print(f"  {p.get('year','????')} {str(p.get('title'))[:66]}")

    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(json.dumps({
        "gold_size": len(gold),
        "union_size": len(ordered),
        "recalls": {str(k): v for k, v in recalls.items()},
        "gate_recall_at_60": gate,
        "gate_pass": gate >= 0.80,
        "per_query": per_query,
        "missed": missed,
    }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Only these gate M2. Everything else can slip.

```
T-001/002 ─▶ T-104 (llm.py + cache) ─▶ T-201..210 (retrieval) ─▶ T-212 (recall gate ≥ 0.80)
                                                                        │
T-301 ─▶ T-302 ─▶ T-303 (Kaggle) ─▶ T-304 (ONNX int8) ──────────┐      │

T-320 ─▶ T-321 ⛔ ─▶ T-322 ─▶ T-323 ─▶ T-324 ────────┐            │                    │
        (Phase 3B — parallel data track, no API,      │            │                    │
         no pipeline, does NOT gate M1 or M2)         │            └──▶ T-501..507 ─────┴─▶ 🔴 M2 (Sep 2)
                                                       │                                     │
                                                       │                       T-603 (fixture) ─▶ T-607 (Panel 3)
                                                       │                                     │
                                       T-304 ─────────▶ T-325 ★★ ──▶ T-705b ◀── T-705   T-702 (Ablation 2)
                                              (verifier cross-check)      (three-lens table)

T-330 ─▶ T-331 ─▶ T-332 (Kaggle) ─▶ T-333 ─▶ T-334 ─▶ T-335 (adoption gate)
        (Phase 3C — reranker fine-tune. NOT on the critical path at all:
         the pipeline ships with the stock reranker and T-335 is a weight
         swap. A failed run here costs nothing downstream.)

Phase 3B joins the critical path only at T-325, which needs the trained verifier.
Everything before it is independent parsing work. T-321 is the internal blocker:
if the bib-resolution gate fails, T-322..T-325 cannot proceed.

Phase 3C touches the critical path nowhere. It reuses T-321's parser and
T-212's eval harness, and its output is optional by construction (T-335).

Phase 6B (Postgres registry) is likewise off the critical path by design: the
pipeline writes to disk regardless and T-625 falls back to a filesystem scan.
```

## 13. Kill switches — decide these on the date, not in hindsight

| Date | If this has not happened | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| **Aug 28** | Recall@20 < 0.80 | Escalate `bge-small` → `bge-base`. Spend all of Aug 29 on retrieval. Push M1 to Sep 1. |
| **Aug 28** | T-321 bib-resolution gate < 0.95 | The delimiter parse is wrong. Spend half a day fixing it. If it still fails, fall back to **`kdercksen/scireviewgen-csv`** (same splits) before abandoning — do not lose T-325 to one bad mirror. |
| **Aug 29** | Kaggle verifier not trained | Fall back to a **stock** NLI checkpoint in the pipeline and report stock-vs-tuned as future work. The pipeline must never block on training. |
| **Aug 30** | T-322 pairs not produced | Drop the T-324 retrieval gold sets (T-212b) and keep **only** the T-325 cross-check. The cross-check is why this track exists; the retrieval breadth check is a bonus. |
| **Aug 30** | Reranker fine-tune (T-332) not trained, or T-334 shows no out-of-domain gain | **Keep the stock reranker and move on.** The pipeline is unaffected — this was always a weight swap, never a dependency. Report the negative result; a fine-tune that did not help is an honest finding, and the verifier still satisfies the training requirement on its own. |
| **Aug 31** | M1 not landed | **Stop building forward.** Stabilise the linear pipeline, ship the survey, cut the Critic loop to a single pass. |
| **Sep 2** | M2 not landed | Ship the five-agent system without the Critic loop. **The Verifier stays** — it is the graded component; the loop is not. |
| **Sep 4** | Vue not started | Ship Panels 1–3 against the fixture, **plus the minimum HITL surface** — a dropped-claims list with confirm/override writing to `human_overrides`. ⚠️ **HITL can no longer be dropped (T-007, 2026-08-25).** Cut Panel 4's *styling and artefact-download chrome* instead, not its function. |
| **Sep 4** | Phase 6B registry not working | **Cut it entirely.** `GET /api/runs` falls back to a filesystem scan and loses nothing the demo needs — the filesystem already holds everything the registry would store. Revert the deck to Chroma + SQLite instead (`SESSION_CONTEXT.md §7.2`). |
| **Sep 6** | Ablations not run | Ship ablation 2 alone. It is the graded claim. Report the rest as future work. |

Gone through it. Here's the picture.

## What this is

**ResearchGPT** — a multi-agent agentic RAG system that produces automated literature reviews. Academic major project, three authors, target submission **~2026-09-07** (12 days out). Python 3.11+, `src/researchgpt`, installable CLI via Typer.

Unusual and worth noting: the repo is run as a **two-agent workflow** — Claude Code plans/specs/reviews, Cursor (Groq) writes the code, with handoff contracts in `handoffs/`. `TASKLIST.md` is the executable backlog and single source of truth (73KB, 116 tasks).

## Where it actually stands

**29 of 116 tasks done** — Phase 0 (preflight), Phase 1 (skeleton), Phase 2 (retrieval) complete through T-211. 2,631 lines of source. `python -m pytest tests -q` → **19 passed** (69s), verified just now.

Built and working: OpenAlex + arXiv search with DOI normalisation and venue tiering, SQLite metadata DB with DOI dedup, PDF loader, offset-preserving chunker, BGE-small embeddings, Chroma vectorstore, BM25, RRF hybrid fusion, cross-encoder reranker, an LLM client with allowlist enforcement + prompt-hash cache + 429 backoff, and the LangGraph `ReviewState` with deliberate per-field reducers.

Not started: everything from **T-212 onward** — verifier training (Phase 3), SciReviewGen (3B), reranker fine-tune (3C), the six agents (Phase 4), critic loop (5), API + Vue (6), evaluation (7).

The `$0` / open-weight-only rule is genuinely enforced in code, not just documented — `ALLOWED_MODELS` in `core/models.py:38` is checked at config-load *and* before any HTTP request in `core/llm.py`. That's a rare case of a constraint actually being load-bearing.

Schedule-wise you're **ahead**: Phase 2 was budgeted Aug 27–28 and landed Aug 25.

## The blocker, and it's more interesting than it looks

`eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json` — the Phase 2 exit gate — **fails badly**: `Recall@60 = 0.029` against a 0.80 gate. But most of that is a measurement bug, not retrieval quality:

1. **`ordered` is insertion-ordered, not ranked** (`retrieval_eval.py:99`). `ordered[:60]` is just whatever the first two queries returned, so "Recall@60" measures query ordering. Full-union recall is `0.371` — still short, but 13× the reported number. `T-213` item (2) already names this fix.
2. **The eval never touches T-209/T-210.** No hybrid fusion, no reranking. You're gating the pipeline on a component the pipeline doesn't use.
3. **DOI-only matching structurally undercounts.** The arXiv arm mints synthetic `10.48550/arxiv.*` DOIs, so an arXiv preprint can never match its published DOI. Of the 22 misses, most are ACL Anthology (`10.18653/v1/…`) — exactly the papers likeliest to be found as preprints and then scored as misses. Normalised-title matching would separate real misses from this artefact.

Fix those three before spending the `T-213` buffer on `bge-base`, or you'll escalate the embedding model to chase a bug. Note also that TASKLIST:253 already says the gate isn't meaningful until the Planner (T-402) generates real queries — the 15 hand-written ones are a stand-in.

## Two smaller real problems

- **`semantic_scholar` is enabled in `configs/default.yaml:81` but implemented nowhere in `src/`.** `SourcesConfig` has no validator against implemented sources, so it fails silently rather than at config load. §0.2 says it's claimed on 8 slides of the Review-2 deck.
- **`README.md` is 0 bytes.**

Also still open from `handoffs/phase2_complete.md`: no `load_dotenv()` in `Embedder`/`Reranker`, so HF calls run unauthenticated.

## The risk I'd actually watch

**M1 — first complete cited survey — is due Aug 31, five days out**, and none of Phase 4 exists. Phase 3 (verifier training on Kaggle) also hasn't started, and it's the graded component that can never be cut. Both are marked parallel/unattended, which means they *can* overlap — but the Kaggle verifier run needs to be kicked off soon to stay off the critical path. The Aug 29 kill switch (fall back to a stock NLI checkpoint) is the safety net, and it's a good one.

Want me to fix the T-212 harness — rank via the hybrid retriever, add title-fallback matching — and re-run the gate? That's the highest-leverage thing available before the Planner exists.

# Test-Driven Development (TDD)

## Overview

Write the test first. Watch it fail. Write minimal code to pass.

**Core principle:** If you didn't watch the test fail, you don't know if it tests the right thing.

**Violating the letter of the rules is violating the spirit of the rules.**

## When to Use

**Always:**
- New features
- Bug fixes
- Refactoring
- Behavior changes

**Exceptions (ask your human partner):**
- Throwaway prototypes
- Generated code
- Configuration files

Thinking "skip TDD just this once"? Stop. That's rationalization.

## The Iron Law

```
NO PRODUCTION CODE WITHOUT A FAILING TEST FIRST
```

Write code before the test? Delete it. Start over.

**No exceptions:**
- Don't keep it as "reference"
- Don't "adapt" it while writing tests
- Don't look at it
- Delete means delete

Implement fresh from tests. Period.

## Red-Green-Refactor

```dot
digraph tdd_cycle {
    rankdir=LR;
    red [label="RED\nWrite failing test", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ffcccc"];
    verify_red [label="Verify fails\ncorrectly", shape=diamond];
    green [label="GREEN\nMinimal code", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccffcc"];
    verify_green [label="Verify passes\nAll green", shape=diamond];
    refactor [label="REFACTOR\nClean up", shape=box, style=filled, fillcolor="#ccccff"];
    next [label="Next", shape=ellipse];

    red -> verify_red;
    verify_red -> green [label="yes"];
    verify_red -> red [label="wrong\nfailure"];
    green -> verify_green;
    verify_green -> refactor [label="yes"];
    verify_green -> green [label="no"];
    refactor -> verify_green [label="stay\ngreen"];
    verify_green -> next;
    next -> red;
}
```

### RED - Write Failing Test

Write one minimal test showing what should happen.

<Good>
```typescript
test('retries failed operations 3 times', async () => {
  let attempts = 0;
  const operation = () => {
    attempts++;
    if (attempts < 3) throw new Error('fail');
    return 'success';
  };

  const result = await retryOperation(operation);

  expect(result).toBe('success');
  expect(attempts).toBe(3);
});
```
Clear name, tests real behavior, one thing
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
test('retry works', async () => {
  const mock = jest.fn()
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockRejectedValueOnce(new Error())
    .mockResolvedValueOnce('success');
  await retryOperation(mock);
  expect(mock).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(3);
});
```
Vague name, tests mock not code
</Bad>

**Requirements:**
- One behavior
- Clear name
- Real code (no mocks unless unavoidable)

### Verify RED - Watch It Fail

**MANDATORY. Never skip.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test fails (not errors)
- Failure message is expected
- Fails because feature missing (not typos)

**Test passes?** You're testing existing behavior. Fix test.

**Test errors?** Fix error, re-run until it fails correctly.

### GREEN - Minimal Code

Write simplest code to pass the test.

<Good>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(fn: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
  for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) {
    try {
      return await fn();
    } catch (e) {
      if (i === 2) throw e;
    }
  }
  throw new Error('unreachable');
}
```
Just enough to pass
</Good>

<Bad>
```typescript
async function retryOperation<T>(
  fn: () => Promise<T>,
  options?: {
    maxRetries?: number;
    backoff?: 'linear' | 'exponential';
    onRetry?: (attempt: number) => void;
  }
): Promise<T> {
  // YAGNI
}
```
Over-engineered
</Bad>

Don't add features, refactor other code, or "improve" beyond the test.

### Verify GREEN - Watch It Pass

**MANDATORY.**

```bash
npm test path/to/test.test.ts
```

Confirm:
- Test passes
- Other tests still pass
- Output pristine (no errors, warnings)

**Test fails?** Fix code, not test.

**Other tests fail?** Fix now.

### REFACTOR - Clean Up

After green only:
- Remove duplication
- Improve names
- Extract helpers

Keep tests green. Don't add behavior.

### Repeat

Next failing test for next feature.

## Good Tests

| Quality | Good | Bad |
|---------|------|-----|
| **Minimal** | One thing. "and" in name? Split it. | `test('validates email and domain and whitespace')` |
| **Clear** | Name describes behavior | `test('test1')` |
| **Shows intent** | Demonstrates desired API | Obscures what code should do |

When writing or changing any test, read [writing-good-tests.md](writing-good-tests.md) for the rules that keep tests honest:
- Name the production change that would make the test fail — before writing it
- Assert on real behavior, never on mock behavior
- Keep test-only code in test utilities, out of production classes
- Understand a dependency's side effects before mocking it

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Too simple to test" | Simple code breaks. Test takes 30 seconds. |
| "I'll test after" | Tests written after pass immediately — which proves nothing. They may test the wrong thing, test the implementation instead of the behavior, or miss the edge case you forgot. You never watched it fail, so you never proved it can catch the bug. Test-first forces that failure. |
| "Tests after achieve same goals (spirit not ritual)" | Tests-after answer "what does this do?"; tests-first answer "what should this do?" Tests written after are biased by the code you already wrote — you verify the cases you remembered, not the ones you'd have discovered. Coverage without proof the tests work. |
| "Already manually tested" | Manual testing is ad-hoc: no record of what you covered, no way to re-run it when the code changes, easy to forget cases under pressure. "Worked when I tried it" ≠ comprehensive. Automated tests run the same way every time. |
| "Deleting X hours is wasteful" | Sunk cost fallacy — that time is already spent either way. The real choice: rewrite with TDD (high confidence) vs. keep it and bolt tests on after (low confidence, likely bugs). Keeping code you can't trust is the waste. |
| "Keep as reference, write tests first" | You'll adapt it. That's testing after. Delete means delete. |
| "Need to explore first" | Fine. Throw away exploration, start with TDD. |
| "Test hard = design unclear" | Listen to test. Hard to test = hard to use. |
| "TDD will slow me down" | TDD IS the pragmatic path: catches bugs before commit, prevents regressions, lets you refactor without fear. "Pragmatic" shortcuts mean debugging in production — slower, not faster. |
| "Manual test faster" | Manual doesn't prove edge cases. You'll re-test every change. |
| "Existing code has no tests" | You're improving it. Add tests for existing code. |

## Red Flags - STOP and Start Over

- Code before test
- Test after implementation
- Test passes immediately
- Can't explain why test failed
- Tests added "later"
- Rationalizing "just this once"
- "I already manually tested it"
- "Tests after achieve the same purpose"
- "It's about spirit not ritual"
- "Keep as reference" or "adapt existing code"
- "Already spent X hours, deleting is wasteful"
- "TDD is dogmatic, I'm being pragmatic"
- "This is different because..."

**All of these mean: Delete code. Start over with TDD.**

## Example: Bug Fix

**Bug:** Empty email accepted

**RED**
```typescript
test('rejects empty email', async () => {
  const result = await submitForm({ email: '' });
  expect(result.error).toBe('Email required');
});
```

**Verify RED**
```bash
$ npm test
FAIL: expected 'Email required', got undefined
```

**GREEN**
```typescript
function submitForm(data: FormData) {
  if (!data.email?.trim()) {
    return { error: 'Email required' };
  }
  // ...
}
```

**Verify GREEN**
```bash
$ npm test
PASS
```

**REFACTOR**
Extract validation for multiple fields if needed.

## Verification Checklist

Before marking work complete:

- [ ] Every new function/method has a test
- [ ] Watched each test fail before implementing
- [ ] Each test failed for expected reason (feature missing, not typo)
- [ ] Wrote minimal code to pass each test
- [ ] All tests pass
- [ ] Output pristine (no errors, warnings)
- [ ] Tests use real code (mocks only if unavoidable)
- [ ] Edge cases and errors covered

Can't check all boxes? You skipped TDD. Start over.

## When Stuck

| Problem | Solution |
|---------|----------|
| Don't know how to test | Write wished-for API. Write assertion first. Ask your human partner. |
| Test too complicated | Design too complicated. Simplify interface. |
| Must mock everything | Code too coupled. Use dependency injection. |
| Test setup huge | Extract helpers. Still complex? Simplify design. |

## Debugging Integration

Bug found? Write failing test reproducing it. Follow TDD cycle. Test proves fix and prevents regression.

Never fix bugs without a test.

## Final Rule

```
Production code → test exists and failed first
Otherwise → not TDD
```

No exceptions without your human partner's permission.

        "externalIds",

#: acceptance suite can zero it out instead of sleeping through a 60s storm.
_BACKOFF_SCHEDULE: tuple[float, ...] = (2.0, 4.0, 8.0, 16.0, 30.0)
_S2_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 6
#: S2 asks for politeness even when requests succeed.
_POLITE_SLEEP_S: float = 1.0

#: S2 caps ``limit`` at 100 per page.
_S2_MAX_LIMIT = 100


def search_semantic_scholar(
    query: str,
    *,
    year_min: int | None = None,
    max_results: int = 25,
    api_key: str | None = None,
    _transport: Any = None,
) -> list[Paper]:
    """Search Semantic Scholar. Best-effort: never raises, may return ``[]``.

    ``api_key`` falls back to ``S2_API_KEY`` in the environment; absent is the
    normal case and only costs reliability, not correctness.

    ``_transport`` is a private test seam (an ``httpx`` transport) so the
    acceptance suite can exercise the 429 path without a live storm. It is not
    part of the T-214 contract - do not depend on it from pipeline code.
    """
    key = api_key or os.getenv("S2_API_KEY") or None
    headers = {"x-api-key": key} if key else {}

    papers: list[Paper] = []
    offset = 0

    with httpx.Client(
        timeout=60.0, follow_redirects=True, headers=headers, transport=_transport
    ) as client:
        while len(papers) < max_results:
            limit = min(_S2_MAX_LIMIT, max_results - len(papers))

                "limit": limit,
                "offset": offset,

"""Reciprocal Rank Fusion hybrid retriever (dense + BM25)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk, RetrievalConfig
from researchgpt.data.bm25_index import BM25Index
from researchgpt.data.embeddings import Embedder
from researchgpt.data.vectorstore import VectorStore


def rrf_fuse(
    rankings: list[list[str]], rrf_k: int = 60
) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    """Pure RRF: score(d) = Σ 1/(rrf_k + rank(d)), rank 1-based."""
    scores: dict[str, float] = {}
    for ranking in rankings:
        for rank_zero, doc_id in enumerate(ranking):
            scores[doc_id] = scores.get(doc_id, 0.0) + 1.0 / (rrf_k + rank_zero + 1)
    return sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)


class HybridRetriever:
    def __init__(
        self,
        store: VectorStore,
        bm25: BM25Index,
        embedder: Embedder,
        cfg: RetrievalConfig,
    ) -> None:
        self._store = store
        self._bm25 = bm25
        self._embedder = embedder
        self._cfg = cfg

    def retrieve(self, query: str) -> list[tuple[Chunk, float]]:
        q_emb = self._embedder.encode_query(query)
        dense = self._store.query(q_emb, k=self._cfg.dense_k)
        sparse = self._bm25.query(query, k=self._cfg.sparse_k)
        dense_ids = [cid for cid, _ in dense]
        sparse_ids = [cid for cid, _ in sparse]
        fused = rrf_fuse([dense_ids, sparse_ids], rrf_k=self._cfg.rrf_k)
        out: list[tuple[Chunk, float]] = []
        for cid, score in fused:
            chunk = self._store.get_chunk(cid)
            if chunk is not None:
                out.append((chunk, score))
        return out


__all__ = ["rrf_fuse", "HybridRetriever"]
"""CPU cross-encoder reranker. Model path is a constructor argument."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk


class Reranker:
    def __init__(
        self,
        model_name: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2",
        device: str = "cpu",
        batch_size: int = 16,
    ) -> None:
        self._model_name = model_name
        self._device = device
        self._batch_size = batch_size
        self._model = CrossEncoder(model_name, device=device)
        self._last_latency_ms = 0

    @property
    def last_latency_ms(self) -> int:
        return self._last_latency_ms

    def rerank(
        self, query: str, chunks: list[Chunk], top_k: int = 12
    ) -> list[tuple[Chunk, float]]:
        if not chunks:
            return []
        pairs = [(query, c.text) for c in chunks]
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        scores = self._model.predict(pairs, batch_size=self._batch_size)
        self._last_latency_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
        ranked = sorted(
            zip(chunks, (float(s) for s in scores), strict=True),
            key=lambda x: x[1],
            reverse=True,
        )
        return ranked[:top_k]


__all__ = ["Reranker"]
"""BM25 sparse index over chunks, persistable to disk."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pickle
import re
from pathlib import Path

from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi

from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk

_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def _tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return [t for t in _TOKEN_RE.split(text.lower()) if t]


class BM25Index:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._bm25: BM25Okapi | None = None
        self._chunk_ids: list[str] = []
        self._corpus_tokens: list[list[str]] = []

    def build(self, chunks: list[Chunk]) -> None:
        self._chunk_ids = [c.chunk_id for c in chunks]
        self._corpus_tokens = [_tokenize(c.text) for c in chunks]
        if not self._corpus_tokens:
            self._bm25 = None
            return
        self._bm25 = BM25Okapi(self._corpus_tokens)

    def query(self, text: str, k: int = 30) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
        if self._bm25 is None or not self._chunk_ids:
            return []
        tokens = _tokenize(text)
        scores = self._bm25.get_scores(tokens)
        paired = list(zip(self._chunk_ids, (float(s) for s in scores), strict=True))
        paired.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        return paired[:k]

    def save(self, path: str = "data/bm25.pkl") -> None:
        p = Path(path)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with p.open("wb") as fh:
            pickle.dump(
                {
                    "chunk_ids": self._chunk_ids,
                    "corpus_tokens": self._corpus_tokens,
                },
                fh,
            )

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str = "data/bm25.pkl") -> BM25Index:
        idx = cls()

"""Reciprocal Rank Fusion hybrid retriever (dense + BM25)."""

from __future__ import annotations

from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk, RetrievalConfig
from researchgpt.data.bm25_index import BM25Index
from researchgpt.data.embeddings import Embedder
from researchgpt.data.vectorstore import VectorStore


def rrf_fuse(
    rankings: list[list[str]], rrf_k: int = 60
) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
    """Pure RRF: score(d) = Σ 1/(rrf_k + rank(d)), rank 1-based."""
    scores: dict[str, float] = {}
    for ranking in rankings:
        for rank_zero, doc_id in enumerate(ranking):
            scores[doc_id] = scores.get(doc_id, 0.0) + 1.0 / (rrf_k + rank_zero + 1)
    return sorted(scores.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)


class HybridRetriever:
    def __init__(
        self,
        store: VectorStore,
        bm25: BM25Index,
        embedder: Embedder,
        cfg: RetrievalConfig,
    ) -> None:
        self._store = store
        self._bm25 = bm25
        self._embedder = embedder
        self._cfg = cfg

    def retrieve(self, query: str) -> list[tuple[Chunk, float]]:
        q_emb = self._embedder.encode_query(query)
        dense = self._store.query(q_emb, k=self._cfg.dense_k)
        sparse = self._bm25.query(query, k=self._cfg.sparse_k)
        dense_ids = [cid for cid, _ in dense]
        sparse_ids = [cid for cid, _ in sparse]
        fused = rrf_fuse([dense_ids, sparse_ids], rrf_k=self._cfg.rrf_k)
        out: list[tuple[Chunk, float]] = []
        for cid, score in fused:
            chunk = self._store.get_chunk(cid)
            if chunk is not None:
                out.append((chunk, score))
        return out


__all__ = ["rrf_fuse", "HybridRetriever"]
"""CPU cross-encoder reranker. Model path is a constructor argument."""

from __future__ import annotations

import time

from sentence_transformers import CrossEncoder

from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk


class Reranker:
    def __init__(
        self,
        model_name: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2",
        device: str = "cpu",
        batch_size: int = 16,
    ) -> None:
        self._model_name = model_name
        self._device = device
        self._batch_size = batch_size
        self._model = CrossEncoder(model_name, device=device)
        self._last_latency_ms = 0

    @property
    def last_latency_ms(self) -> int:
        return self._last_latency_ms

    def rerank(
        self, query: str, chunks: list[Chunk], top_k: int = 12
    ) -> list[tuple[Chunk, float]]:
        if not chunks:
            return []
        pairs = [(query, c.text) for c in chunks]
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        scores = self._model.predict(pairs, batch_size=self._batch_size)
        self._last_latency_ms = int((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)
        ranked = sorted(
            zip(chunks, (float(s) for s in scores), strict=True),
            key=lambda x: x[1],
            reverse=True,
        )
        return ranked[:top_k]


__all__ = ["Reranker"]
"""BM25 sparse index over chunks, persistable to disk."""

from __future__ import annotations

import pickle
import re
from pathlib import Path

from rank_bm25 import BM25Okapi

from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk

_TOKEN_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")


def _tokenize(text: str) -> list[str]:
    return [t for t in _TOKEN_RE.split(text.lower()) if t]


class BM25Index:
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._bm25: BM25Okapi | None = None
        self._chunk_ids: list[str] = []
        self._corpus_tokens: list[list[str]] = []

    def build(self, chunks: list[Chunk]) -> None:
        self._chunk_ids = [c.chunk_id for c in chunks]
        self._corpus_tokens = [_tokenize(c.text) for c in chunks]
        if not self._corpus_tokens:
            self._bm25 = None
            return
        self._bm25 = BM25Okapi(self._corpus_tokens)

    def query(self, text: str, k: int = 30) -> list[tuple[str, float]]:
        if self._bm25 is None or not self._chunk_ids:
            return []
        tokens = _tokenize(text)
        scores = self._bm25.get_scores(tokens)
        paired = list(zip(self._chunk_ids, (float(s) for s in scores), strict=True))
        paired.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
        return paired[:k]

    def save(self, path: str = "data/bm25.pkl") -> None:
        p = Path(path)
        p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        with p.open("wb") as fh:
            pickle.dump(
                {
                    "chunk_ids": self._chunk_ids,
                    "corpus_tokens": self._corpus_tokens,
                },
                fh,
            )

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: str = "data/bm25.pkl") -> BM25Index:
        idx = cls()
        with Path(path).open("rb") as fh:
            data = pickle.load(fh)
        idx._chunk_ids = data["chunk_ids"]
        idx._corpus_tokens = data["corpus_tokens"]
        if idx._corpus_tokens:
            idx._bm25 = BM25Okapi(idx._corpus_tokens)
        return idx


__all__ = ["BM25Index"]

"""T-212 — retrieval recall against the project's own bibliography.

Measures whether the corpus builder finds the papers a human curator found.

**Gate.** `PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.2` specifies "Recall@20 >= 0.80". With a 35-paper
gold set that is unachievable: retrieving 20 papers caps recall at 20/35 = 0.57.
The corrected gate (TASKLIST T-212) is **Recall@60 >= 0.80**, where 60 is
``review.max_papers`` — the corpus the Extractor actually sees and therefore the
thing downstream quality depends on. Recall@20 is still reported as a secondary
diagnostic, labelled with its ceiling.

**Two corrections applied 2026-08-26 (T-213 items 2 and 3).** The first run of
this harness reported ``Recall@60 = 0.029`` and that number was mostly an
artefact of the harness, not of retrieval:

1. *The cut-off ranked nothing.* The union was ordered by the sequence in which
   queries happened to run, so ``union[:60]`` meant "everything the first two
   queries returned" rather than "the best 60 papers". Recall over the whole
   447-paper union was 0.371 — 13x the reported gate number. The corpus is now
   **ranked through the real T-209 hybrid retriever and T-210 cross-encoder
   reranker**, then merged across sub-questions round-robin by rank, which is
   how the Retriever agent (T-403) will build it.
2. *DOI-only matching undercounts by construction.* arXiv records carry the
   synthetic ``10.48550/arxiv.*`` join key, so retrieving the preprint of a
   published paper scored as a miss. Of the original 22 misses, most were ACL
   Anthology papers — exactly the population most likely to be found as
   preprints. Recall is now reported **both ways**: DOI-only (conservative) and
   DOI-or-normalised-title (the honest "did we find this paper" number). Both
   are printed; neither is hidden.

Semantic Scholar (T-214) joins OpenAlex and arXiv here as a best-effort third
source. It is throttled without a key (T-215), and when it is, it contributes
nothing and the eval continues — that is the designed behaviour, not a failure.

⚠️ **Sequencing.** TASKLIST T-212 notes this gate is not final until the Planner
(T-402) exists, because recall is dominated by query generation. The queries
below are a hand-written stand-in for it. Re-run after T-402 and treat *that* as
the real Phase 2 gate.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval [--max-per-source N] [--no-rank]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import tempfile
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk, Paper
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import (
    search_arxiv,
    search_openalex,
    search_semantic_scholar,
)

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")

_TITLE_NOISE_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")

#: Stands in for the Planner (T-402), which does not exist yet. These mirror
#: the six thematic clusters of the literature review (SPEC §1.6) so the
#: evaluation reflects the real multi-sub-question retrieval pattern rather
#: than a single lucky query.
QUERIES = [
    # SHORT queries — 2-4 terms. OpenAlex ANDs every term in
    # title_and_abstract.search, so a 6-term query matches almost nothing
    # (measured 2026-08-25: "scientific claim verification evidence entailment
    # SciFact" -> 0 results; "scientific claim verification" -> 4,174).
    # This constraint must be reflected in the Planner prompt (T-402).
    "agentic retrieval augmented generation",
    "automated literature review generation",
    "scientific survey generation",
    "scientific claim verification",
    "citation accuracy language models",
    "hallucination large language models",
    "retrieval augmented generation evaluation",
    "multi-agent large language model",
    "systematic review automation",
    "cross-encoder reranking retrieval",
    "attributed question answering citations",
    "scientific information extraction",
    "citation text generation",
    "evidence retrieval fact checking",
    "RAG survey",
]


def norm(doi: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not doi:
        return None
    return doi.strip().lower().replace("https://doi.org/", "")


def norm_title(title: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Aggressive title key so an arXiv preprint matches its published version.

    Collapses to lowercase alphanumerics. Short titles are dropped — a 3-word
    key collides too easily, and a false *hit* flatters the gate in the one
    direction that matters.
    """
    if not title:
        return None
    key = _TITLE_NOISE_RE.sub("", title.lower())
    return key if len(key) >= 25 else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corpus construction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def gather(query: str, *, year_min: int, max_per_source: int) -> list[Paper]:
    """All three connectors for one sub-question. Never raises."""
    papers: list[Paper] = []
    for name, fn in (
        ("openalex", lambda: search_openalex(query, year_min=year_min, max_results=max_per_source)),
        ("arxiv", lambda: search_arxiv(query, max_results=max(10, max_per_source // 2))),
        (
            "semantic_scholar",
            lambda: search_semantic_scholar(
                query, year_min=year_min, max_results=max_per_source
            ),
        ),
    ):
        try:
            papers += fn()
        except Exception as exc:  # a source outage must not end the eval
            print(f"    {name} failed on {query[:36]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)
    return papers


def paper_key(p: Paper) -> str:
    """Stable identity for a retrieved record: DOI when present, else title."""
    return norm(p.doi) or norm_title(p.title) or f"{p.source}:{p.paper_id}"


def as_chunk(key: str, p: Paper) -> Chunk:
    """One pseudo-chunk per paper: title + abstract is what a corpus-selection
    decision is actually made on, so that is what gets ranked."""
    text = p.title if not p.abstract else f"{p.title}\n\n{p.abstract}"
    return Chunk(
        chunk_id=key,
        paper_id=key,
        text=text,
        section="abstract",
        start_char=0,
        end_char=len(text),
    )


def rank_corpus(
    per_query: dict[str, list[str]],
    pool: dict[str, Paper],
    cfg: Any,
) -> list[str]:
    """T-213(2) — rank the pool through the real T-209 + T-210 stack.

    Each sub-question is ranked independently, then merged round-robin by rank
    so every sub-question contributes to the head of the corpus. That is the
    policy the Retriever agent needs anyway: a corpus that answers one
    sub-question perfectly and five not at all fails coverage downstream.
    """
    # Imported here: these pull torch, and --no-rank must stay usable without it.
    from researchgpt.data.bm25_index import BM25Index
    from researchgpt.data.embeddings import Embedder
    from researchgpt.data.vectorstore import VectorStore
    from researchgpt.tools.hybrid_retriever import HybridRetriever
    from researchgpt.tools.reranker import Reranker

    chunks = [as_chunk(k, p) for k, p in pool.items()]
    print(f"\nranking {len(chunks)} pooled papers through T-209 + T-210 ...", flush=True)

    embedder = Embedder(
        model_name=cfg.embeddings.model,
        device=cfg.embeddings.device,
        batch_size=cfg.embeddings.batch_size,
    )
    embeddings = embedder.encode([c.text for c in chunks])

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True) as tmp:
        store = VectorStore(path=tmp, collection="t212")
        store.add(chunks, embeddings)
        bm25 = BM25Index()
        bm25.build(chunks)
        retriever = HybridRetriever(store, bm25, embedder, cfg.retrieval)
        reranker = Reranker(model_name=cfg.retrieval.reranker, device=cfg.embeddings.device)

        ranked_per_query: list[list[str]] = []
        for query in QUERIES:
            fused = retriever.retrieve(query)
            # Restrict to what this sub-question actually retrieved from the
            # live sources; the pool is shared, the attribution is not.
            allowed = set(per_query.get(query, ()))
            candidates = [c for c, _ in fused if c.chunk_id in allowed]
            if not candidates:
                ranked_per_query.append([])
                continue
            top = reranker.rerank(query, candidates, top_k=len(candidates))
            ranked_per_query.append([c.chunk_id for c, _ in top])
        print(f"  reranker last batch: {reranker.last_latency_ms} ms", flush=True)

        store.reset()

    # Round-robin merge by rank.
    ordered: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    depth = max((len(r) for r in ranked_per_query), default=0)
    for i in range(depth):
        for ranking in ranked_per_query:
            if i < len(ranking) and ranking[i] not in seen:
                seen.add(ranking[i])
                ordered.append(ranking[i])
    # Anything no sub-question ranked still belongs in the union tail.
    for key in pool:
        if key not in seen:
            ordered.append(key)
    return ordered


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def recall_at(ordered: list[str], pool: dict[str, Paper], gold_dois: set[str],
              gold_titles: set[str], k: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """(doi_only, doi_or_title) recall over the first ``k`` ranked papers."""
    top = ordered[:k]
    hit_doi: set[str] = set()
    hit_any: set[str] = set()
    for key in top:
        p = pool[key]
        d = norm(p.doi)
        t = norm_title(p.title)
        if d and d in gold_dois:
            hit_doi.add(d)
            hit_any.add(d)
        elif t and t in gold_titles:
            hit_any.add(gold_titles[t] if isinstance(gold_titles, dict) else t)
    denom = len(gold_dois) or 1
    return len(hit_doi) / denom, len(hit_any) / denom


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--max-per-source",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        help="T-213(3): override sources.max_per_source and re-measure.",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--no-rank",
        action="store_true",
        help="Skip T-209/T-210 ranking and use raw insertion order (the old, "
             "broken behaviour — kept only to reproduce the 2026-08-25 number).",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    max_per_source = args.max_per_source or cfg.sources.max_per_source

    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    gold_dois = {norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    gold_dois.discard(None)
    # normalised title -> gold DOI, so a title hit resolves to the same identity
    gold_title_to_doi: dict[str, str] = {}
    for p in gold_doc["papers"]:
        t, d = norm_title(p.get("title")), norm(p.get("doi"))
        if t and d:
            gold_title_to_doi[t] = d

    print(f"gold set: {len(gold_dois)} DOIs ({len(gold_title_to_doi)} with usable titles)")
    print(f"max_per_source: {max_per_source}   ranking: {'off' if args.no_rank else 'on'}\n")

    pool: dict[str, Paper] = {}
    per_query: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    insertion_order: list[str] = []
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for query in QUERIES:
        papers = gather(query, year_min=cfg.review.year_min, max_per_source=max_per_source)
        keys: list[str] = []
        sources_seen: set[str] = set()
        for p in papers:
            key = paper_key(p)
            sources_seen.add(p.source)
            if key not in pool:
                pool[key] = p
                insertion_order.append(key)
            elif not pool[key].abstract and p.abstract:
                pool[key] = p  # prefer the record that carries an abstract
            if key not in keys:
                keys.append(key)
        per_query[query] = keys
        hits = sum(
            1
            for k in keys
            if (norm(pool[k].doi) in gold_dois)
            or (norm_title(pool[k].title) in gold_title_to_doi)
        )
        rows.append(
            {
                "query": query,
                "retrieved": len(keys),
                "gold_hits": hits,
                "sources": sorted(sources_seen),
            }
        )
        print(f"  {hits:2d} gold hits / {len(keys):3d} unique  |  {query[:46]}", flush=True)

    ordered = insertion_order if args.no_rank else rank_corpus(per_query, pool, cfg)

    cutoffs = [20, 40, 60, 100, len(ordered)]
    recalls: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    for k in cutoffs:
        if k <= 0:
            continue
        doi_only, any_match = recall_at(ordered, pool, gold_dois, gold_title_to_doi, k)
        recalls[str(k)] = {"doi_only": doi_only, "doi_or_title": any_match}

    print(f"\nunion corpus: {len(ordered)} unique papers across {len(QUERIES)} queries")
    print("\nRECALL                doi-only   doi-or-title")
    for k_str, vals in recalls.items():
        k = int(k_str)
        ceiling = min(k, len(gold_dois)) / len(gold_dois)
        note = f"  [ceiling {ceiling:.2f}]" if ceiling < 1.0 else ""
        gate = "  <- GATE (max_papers)" if k == 60 else ""
        print(
            f"  Recall@{k:<6d}      {vals['doi_only']:.3f }      "
            f"{vals['doi_or_title']:.3f}{note}{gate}"
        )

    gate = recalls.get("60", {}).get("doi_or_title", 0.0)
    gate_doi = recalls.get("60", {}).get("doi_only", 0.0)
    verdict = "PASS" if gate >= 0.80 else "FAIL"
    print(f"\nGATE  Recall@60 >= 0.80  ->  {gate:.3f} (doi-or-title)  {verdict}")
    print(f"      doi-only equivalent: {gate_doi:.3f}")

    # What the whole union never found at all — these bound every downstream metric.
    found: set[str] = set()
    for key in ordered:
        p = pool[key]
        d, t = norm(p.doi), norm_title(p.title)
        if d and d in gold_dois:
            found.add(d)
        elif t and t in gold_title_to_doi:
            found.add(gold_title_to_doi[t])
    missed = sorted(gold_dois - found)
    print(f"\nfound {len(found)}/{len(gold_dois)} gold papers anywhere in the union; "
          f"missed {len(missed)}")
    if missed:
        by_doi = {norm(p["doi"]): p for p in gold_doc["papers"]}
        print("\nNEVER RETRIEVED (bounds every downstream metric):")
        for d in missed[:15]:
            p = by_doi.get(d, {})
            print(f"  {p.get('year', '????')} {str(p.get('title'))[:66]}")

    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "generated": "T-212 (harness corrected 2026-08-26; see module docstring)",
                "ranked": not args.no_rank,
                "max_per_source": max_per_source,
                "gold_size": len(gold_dois),
                "union_size": len(ordered),
                "recalls": recalls,
                "gate_recall_at_60": gate,
                "gate_recall_at_60_doi_only": gate_doi,
                "gate_pass": gate >= 0.80,
                "per_query": rows,
                "missed": missed,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
