**Gate.** `PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.2` specifies "Recall@20 >= 0.80". With a 35-paper
gold set that is unachievable: retrieving 20 papers caps recall at 20/35 = 0.57.
The corrected gate (TASKLIST T-212) is **Recall@60 >= 0.80**, where 60 is
``review.max_papers`` — the corpus the Extractor actually sees and therefore the
thing downstream quality depends on. Recall@20 is still reported as a secondary
diagnostic, labelled with its ceiling.

**Two corrections applied 2026-08-26 (T-213 items 2 and 3).** The first run of
this harness reported ``Recall@60 = 0.029`` and that number was mostly an
artefact of the harness, not of retrieval:

1. *The cut-off ranked nothing.* The union was ordered by the sequence in which
   queries happened to run, so ``union[:60]`` meant "everything the first two
   queries returned" rather than "the best 60 papers". Recall over the whole
   447-paper union was 0.371 — 13x the reported gate number. The corpus is now
   **ranked through the real T-209 hybrid retriever and T-210 cross-encoder
   reranker**, then merged across sub-questions round-robin by rank, which is
   how the Retriever agent (T-403) will build it.
2. *DOI-only matching undercounts by construction.* arXiv records carry the
   synthetic ``10.48550/arxiv.*`` join key, so retrieving the preprint of a
   published paper scored as a miss. Of the original 22 misses, most were ACL
   Anthology papers — exactly the population most likely to be found as
   preprints. Recall is now reported **both ways**: DOI-only (conservative) and
   DOI-or-normalised-title (the honest "did we find this paper" number). Both
   are printed; neither is hidden.

Semantic Scholar (T-214) joins OpenAlex and arXiv here as a best-effort third
source. It is throttled without a key (T-215), and when it is, it contributes
nothing and the eval continues — that is the designed behaviour, not a failure.

⚠️ **Sequencing.** TASKLIST T-212 notes this gate is not final until the Planner
(T-402) exists, because recall is dominated by query generation. The queries
below are a hand-written stand-in for it. Re-run after T-402 and treat *that* as
the real Phase 2 gate.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval [--max-per-source N] [--no-rank]
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import tempfile
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.core.models import Chunk, Paper
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import (
    search_arxiv,
    search_openalex,
    search_semantic_scholar,
)

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")

_TITLE_NOISE_RE = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")

#: Stands in for the Planner (T-402), which does not exist yet. These mirror
#: the six thematic clusters of the literature review (SPEC §1.6) so the
#: evaluation reflects the real multi-sub-question retrieval pattern rather
#: than a single lucky query.
QUERIES = [
    # SHORT queries — 2-4 terms. OpenAlex ANDs every term in
    # title_and_abstract.search, so a 6-term query matches almost nothing
    # (measured 2026-08-25: "scientific claim verification evidence entailment
    # SciFact" -> 0 results; "scientific claim verification" -> 4,174).
    # This constraint must be reflected in the Planner prompt (T-402).
    "agentic retrieval augmented generation",
    "automated literature review generation",
    "scientific survey generation",
    "scientific claim verification",
    "citation accuracy language models",
    "hallucination large language models",
    "retrieval augmented generation evaluation",
    "multi-agent large language model",
    "systematic review automation",
    "cross-encoder reranking retrieval",
    "attributed question answering citations",
    "scientific information extraction",
    "citation text generation",
    "evidence retrieval fact checking",
    "RAG survey",
]


def norm(doi: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not doi:
        return None
    return doi.strip().lower().replace("https://doi.org/", "")


def norm_title(title: str | None) -> str | None:
    """Aggressive title key so an arXiv preprint matches its published version.

    Collapses to lowercase alphanumerics. Short titles are dropped — a 3-word
    key collides too easily, and a false *hit* flatters the gate in the one
    direction that matters.
    """
    if not title:
        return None
    key = _TITLE_NOISE_RE.sub("", title.lower())
    return key if len(key) >= 25 else None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corpus construction
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def gather(query: str, *, year_min: int, max_per_source: int) -> list[Paper]:
    """All three connectors for one sub-question. Never raises."""
    papers: list[Paper] = []
    for name, fn in (
        ("openalex", lambda: search_openalex(query, year_min=year_min, max_results=max_per_source)),
        ("arxiv", lambda: search_arxiv(query, max_results=max(10, max_per_source // 2))),
        (
            "semantic_scholar",
            lambda: search_semantic_scholar(
                query, year_min=year_min, max_results=max_per_source
            ),
        ),
    ):
        try:
            papers += fn()
        except Exception as exc:  # a source outage must not end the eval
            print(f"    {name} failed on {query[:36]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)
    return papers


def paper_key(p: Paper) -> str:
    """Stable identity for a retrieved record: DOI when present, else title."""
    return norm(p.doi) or norm_title(p.title) or f"{p.source}:{p.paper_id}"


def as_chunk(key: str, p: Paper) -> Chunk:
    """One pseudo-chunk per paper: title + abstract is what a corpus-selection
    decision is actually made on, so that is what gets ranked."""
    text = p.title if not p.abstract else f"{p.title}\n\n{p.abstract}"
    return Chunk(
        chunk_id=key,
        paper_id=key,
        text=text,
        section="abstract",
        start_char=0,
        end_char=len(text),
    )


def rank_corpus(
    per_query: dict[str, list[str]],
    pool: dict[str, Paper],
    cfg: Any,
) -> list[str]:
    """T-213(2) — rank the pool through the real T-209 + T-210 stack.

    Each sub-question is ranked independently, then merged round-robin by rank
    so every sub-question contributes to the head of the corpus. That is the
    policy the Retriever agent needs anyway: a corpus that answers one
    sub-question perfectly and five not at all fails coverage downstream.
    """
    # Imported here: these pull torch, and --no-rank must stay usable without it.
    from researchgpt.data.bm25_index import BM25Index
    from researchgpt.data.embeddings import Embedder
    from researchgpt.data.vectorstore import VectorStore
    from researchgpt.tools.hybrid_retriever import HybridRetriever
    from researchgpt.tools.reranker import Reranker

    chunks = [as_chunk(k, p) for k, p in pool.items()]
    print(f"\nranking {len(chunks)} pooled papers through T-209 + T-210 ...", flush=True)

    embedder = Embedder(
        model_name=cfg.embeddings.model,
        device=cfg.embeddings.device,
        batch_size=cfg.embeddings.batch_size,
    )
    embeddings = embedder.encode([c.text for c in chunks])

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True) as tmp:
        store = VectorStore(path=tmp, collection="t212")
        store.add(chunks, embeddings)
        bm25 = BM25Index()
        bm25.build(chunks)
        retriever = HybridRetriever(store, bm25, embedder, cfg.retrieval)
        reranker = Reranker(model_name=cfg.retrieval.reranker, device=cfg.embeddings.device)

        ranked_per_query: list[list[str]] = []
        for query in QUERIES:
            fused = retriever.retrieve(query)
            # Restrict to what this sub-question actually retrieved from the
            # live sources; the pool is shared, the attribution is not.
            allowed = set(per_query.get(query, ()))
            candidates = [c for c, _ in fused if c.chunk_id in allowed]
            if not candidates:
                ranked_per_query.append([])
                continue
            top = reranker.rerank(query, candidates, top_k=len(candidates))
            ranked_per_query.append([c.chunk_id for c, _ in top])
        print(f"  reranker last batch: {reranker.last_latency_ms} ms", flush=True)

        store.reset()

    # Round-robin merge by rank.
    ordered: list[str] = []
    seen: set[str] = set()
    depth = max((len(r) for r in ranked_per_query), default=0)
    for i in range(depth):
        for ranking in ranked_per_query:
            if i < len(ranking) and ranking[i] not in seen:
                seen.add(ranking[i])
                ordered.append(ranking[i])
    # Anything no sub-question ranked still belongs in the union tail.
    for key in pool:
        if key not in seen:
            ordered.append(key)
    return ordered


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Scoring
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def recall_at(ordered: list[str], pool: dict[str, Paper], gold_dois: set[str],
              gold_titles: set[str], k: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """(doi_only, doi_or_title) recall over the first ``k`` ranked papers."""
    top = ordered[:k]
    hit_doi: set[str] = set()
    hit_any: set[str] = set()
    for key in top:
        p = pool[key]
        d = norm(p.doi)
        t = norm_title(p.title)
        if d and d in gold_dois:
            hit_doi.add(d)
            hit_any.add(d)
        elif t and t in gold_titles:
            hit_any.add(gold_titles[t] if isinstance(gold_titles, dict) else t)
    denom = len(gold_dois) or 1
    return len(hit_doi) / denom, len(hit_any) / denom


def main() -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument(
        "--max-per-source",
        type=int,
        default=None,
        help="T-213(3): override sources.max_per_source and re-measure.",
    )
    ap.add_argument(
        "--no-rank",
        action="store_true",
        help="Skip T-209/T-210 ranking and use raw insertion order (the old, "
             "broken behaviour — kept only to reproduce the 2026-08-25 number).",
    )
    args = ap.parse_args()

    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    max_per_source = args.max_per_source or cfg.sources.max_per_source

    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    gold_dois = {norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    gold_dois.discard(None)
    # normalised title -> gold DOI, so a title hit resolves to the same identity
    gold_title_to_doi: dict[str, str] = {}
    for p in gold_doc["papers"]:
        t, d = norm_title(p.get("title")), norm(p.get("doi"))
        if t and d:
            gold_title_to_doi[t] = d

    print(f"gold set: {len(gold_dois)} DOIs ({len(gold_title_to_doi)} with usable titles)")
    print(f"max_per_source: {max_per_source}   ranking: {'off' if args.no_rank else 'on'}\n")

    pool: dict[str, Paper] = {}
    per_query: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    insertion_order: list[str] = []
    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    for query in QUERIES:
        papers = gather(query, year_min=cfg.review.year_min, max_per_source=max_per_source)
        keys: list[str] = []
        sources_seen: set[str] = set()
        for p in papers:
            key = paper_key(p)
            sources_seen.add(p.source)
            if key not in pool:
                pool[key] = p
                insertion_order.append(key)
            elif not pool[key].abstract and p.abstract:
                pool[key] = p  # prefer the record that carries an abstract
            if key not in keys:
                keys.append(key)
        per_query[query] = keys
        hits = sum(
            1
            for k in keys
            if (norm(pool[k].doi) in gold_dois)
            or (norm_title(pool[k].title) in gold_title_to_doi)
        )
        rows.append(
            {
                "query": query,
                "retrieved": len(keys),
                "gold_hits": hits,
                "sources": sorted(sources_seen),
            }
        )
        print(f"  {hits:2d} gold hits / {len(keys):3d} unique  |  {query[:46]}", flush=True)

    ordered = insertion_order if args.no_rank else rank_corpus(per_query, pool, cfg)

    cutoffs = [20, 40, 60, 100, len(ordered)]
    recalls: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {}
    for k in cutoffs:
        if k <= 0:
            continue
        doi_only, any_match = recall_at(ordered, pool, gold_dois, gold_title_to_doi, k)
        recalls[str(k)] = {"doi_only": doi_only, "doi_or_title": any_match}

    print(f"\nunion corpus: {len(ordered)} unique papers across {len(QUERIES)} queries")
    print("\nRECALL                doi-only   doi-or-title")
    for k_str, vals in recalls.items():
        k = int(k_str)
        ceiling = min(k, len(gold_dois)) / len(gold_dois)
        note = f"  [ceiling {ceiling:.2f}]" if ceiling < 1.0 else ""
        gate = "  <- GATE (max_papers)" if k == 60 else ""
        print(
            f"  Recall@{k:<6d}      {vals['doi_only']:.3f }      "
            f"{vals['doi_or_title']:.3f}{note}{gate}"
        )

    gate = recalls.get("60", {}).get("doi_or_title", 0.0)
    gate_doi = recalls.get("60", {}).get("doi_only", 0.0)
    verdict = "PASS" if gate >= 0.80 else "FAIL"
    print(f"\nGATE  Recall@60 >= 0.80  ->  {gate:.3f} (doi-or-title)  {verdict}")
    print(f"      doi-only equivalent: {gate_doi:.3f}")

    # What the whole union never found at all — these bound every downstream metric.
    found: set[str] = set()
    for key in ordered:
        p = pool[key]
        d, t = norm(p.doi), norm_title(p.title)
        if d and d in gold_dois:
            found.add(d)
        elif t and t in gold_title_to_doi:
            found.add(gold_title_to_doi[t])
    missed = sorted(gold_dois - found)
    print(f"\nfound {len(found)}/{len(gold_dois)} gold papers anywhere in the union; "
          f"missed {len(missed)}")
    if missed:
        by_doi = {norm(p["doi"]): p for p in gold_doc["papers"]}
        print("\nNEVER RETRIEVED (bounds every downstream metric):")
        for d in missed[:15]:
            p = by_doi.get(d, {})
            print(f"  {p.get('year', '????')} {str(p.get('title'))[:66]}")

    OUT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    OUT.write_text(
        json.dumps(
            {
                "generated": "T-212 (harness corrected 2026-08-26; see module docstring)",
                "ranked": not args.no_rank,
                "max_per_source": max_per_source,
                "gold_size": len(gold_dois),
                "union_size": len(ordered),
                "recalls": recalls,
                "gate_recall_at_60": gate,
                "gate_recall_at_60_doi_only": gate_doi,
                "gate_pass": gate >= 0.80,
                "per_query": rows,
                "missed": missed,
            },
            indent=2,
        ),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""T-212 — retrieval recall against the project's own bibliography.

Measures whether the corpus builder finds the papers a human curator found.

**Gate note.** `PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.2` specifies "Recall@20 >= 0.80". With a
35-paper gold set that is unachievable: retrieving 20 papers caps recall at
20/35 = 0.57. The corrected gate (TASKLIST T-212) is **Recall@60 >= 0.80**,
where 60 is ``review.max_papers`` - the corpus the Extractor actually sees and
therefore the thing downstream quality depends on. Recall@20 is still reported
as a secondary diagnostic, labelled with its ceiling.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import search_arxiv, search_openalex

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")

#: Stands in for the Planner (T-402), which does not exist yet. These mirror
#: the six thematic clusters of the literature review (SPEC §1.6) so the
#: evaluation reflects the real multi-sub-question retrieval pattern rather
#: than a single lucky query.
QUERIES = [
    # SHORT queries — 2-4 terms. OpenAlex ANDs every term in
    # title_and_abstract.search, so a 6-term query matches almost nothing
    # (measured 2026-08-25: "scientific claim verification evidence entailment
    # SciFact" -> 0 results; "scientific claim verification" -> 4,174).
    # This constraint must be reflected in the Planner prompt (T-402).
    "agentic retrieval augmented generation",
    "automated literature review generation",
    "scientific survey generation",
    "scientific claim verification",
    "citation accuracy language models",
    "hallucination large language models",
    "retrieval augmented generation evaluation",
    "multi-agent large language model",
    "systematic review automation",
    "cross-encoder reranking retrieval",
    "attributed question answering citations",
    "scientific information extraction",
    "citation text generation",
    "evidence retrieval fact checking",
    "RAG survey",
]


def norm(doi: str | None) -> str | None:
    if not doi:
        return None
    return doi.strip().lower().replace("https://doi.org/", "")


def main() -> None:
    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    gold = {norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    print(f"gold set: {len(gold)} DOIs\n", flush=True)

    per_query: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    union: dict[str, Any] = {}          # doi -> first rank seen
    ordered: list[str] = []             # dedup order across queries

    for q in QUERIES:
        found: list[str] = []
        try:
            papers = search_openalex(q, year_min=cfg.review.year_min, max_results=25)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  openalex failed on {q[:40]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)
            papers = []
        try:
            papers += search_arxiv(q, max_results=15)
        except Exception as exc:
            print(f"  arxiv failed on {q[:40]!r}: {type(exc).__name__}", flush=True)

        for p in papers:
            d = norm(p.doi)
            if not d:
                continue
            if d not in union:
                union[d] = len(ordered)
                ordered.append(d)
            if d in gold:
                found.append(d)

        hit = len(set(found))
        per_query.append({"query": q, "retrieved": len(papers), "gold_hits": hit})
        print(f"  {hit:2d} gold hits / {len(papers):3d} retrieved  |  {q[:52]}", flush=True)

    # Recall at increasing corpus cut-offs.
    recalls = {}
    for k in (20, 40, 60, 100, len(ordered)):
        if k <= 0:
            continue
        top = set(ordered[:k])
        recalls[k] = len(top & gold) / len(gold)

    found_all = set(ordered) & gold
    missed = sorted(gold - found_all)

        note = f"  [ceiling {ceiling:.2f}]" if ceiling < 1.0 else ""
        print(f"  Recall@{k:<5d} = {v:.3f}{note}{label}", flush=True)

    gate = recalls.get(60, 0.0)
    print(f"\nGATE  Recall@60 >= 0.80  ->  {gate:.3f}  {'PASS' if gate >= 0.80 else 'FAIL'}")

        for d in missed[:15]:
            p = by_doi.get(d, {})
            print(f"  {p.get('year','????')} {str(p.get('title'))[:66]}")

        "union_size": len(ordered),
        "recalls": {str(k): v for k, v in recalls.items()},
        "gate_recall_at_60": gate,
        "gate_pass": gate >= 0.80,
        "per_query": per_query,
        "missed": missed,
    }, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")

"""Core Pydantic data models.

Source of truth: RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §8. Every other module imports its shapes
from here; nothing in this file may import from the rest of the package, so it
stays dependency-free and safe to import anywhere.

Deviations from SPEC §8, all deliberate and recorded in TASKLIST.md:

* ``Paper.text_availability`` is new. TASKLIST T-204 sets it and T-505 enforces
  the abstract-only rule that depends on it (abstract-only papers may be cited
  as existing but may not supply verified claims).
* ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` lives here rather than in ``core/llm.py`` as TASKLIST §0.1
  originally said. Reason: this module has no dependencies, so ``core/config.py``
  can validate model names at config-load time instead of failing at the first
  API call. ``core/llm.py`` still owns *enforcement* — it imports and checks this
  constant before constructing any request.
* ``RunConfig`` and its nested models are new. SPEC §10.1 specifies the YAML but
  never types it, and SPEC's version predates the $0 constraint.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enumerations (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

VenueTier = Literal[
    "scopus_q1", "scopus", "ieee", "acl", "peer_reviewed", "preprint", "unknown"
]
Verdict = Literal["SUPPORTED", "PARTIAL", "UNSUPPORTED", "CONTRADICTED"]
Decision = Literal["WRITE", "RETRIEVE", "REPLAN"]
TextAvailability = Literal["full", "abstract_only", "none"]

#: TASKLIST §0.1 — the $0 hard rule. Only free, open-weight models.
#: Verified live 2026-08-25. ``core/llm.py`` raises on anything not in here.
ALLOWED_MODELS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        # Google AI Studio — open-weight Gemma, free tier
        "gemma-4-31b-it",
        "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
        # Groq — open-weight, free tier
        "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
        "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
        "qwen/qwen3.6-27b",
    }
)

#: Provider inferred from model name; used by ``core/llm.py`` to pick a client.
MODEL_PROVIDER: dict[str, str] = {
    "gemma-4-31b-it": "google",
    "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it": "google",
    "openai/gpt-oss-120b": "groq",
    "openai/gpt-oss-20b": "groq",
    "qwen/qwen3.6-27b": "groq",
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corpus models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Paper(BaseModel):
    paper_id: str
    doi: Optional[str] = None
    title: str
    authors: list[str] = []
    year: Optional[int] = None
    venue: Optional[str] = None
    venue_tier: VenueTier = "unknown"
    abstract: Optional[str] = None
    url: Optional[str] = None
    pdf_path: Optional[str] = None
    source: str  # openalex | arxiv
    citation_count: Optional[int] = None
    is_preprint: bool = False
    #: Set by the PDF loader (T-204). Gates claim sourcing under T-505.
    text_availability: TextAvailability = "none"


class Chunk(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    paper_id: str
    text: str
    section: Optional[str] = None  # abstract | methods | results | ...
    start_char: int
    end_char: int
    embedding_id: Optional[str] = None

    @field_validator("end_char")
    @classmethod
    def _end_after_start(cls, v: int, info) -> int:
        start = info.data.get("start_char")
        if start is not None and v < start:
            raise ValueError(f"end_char {v} precedes start_char {start}")
        return v


class EvidenceSpan(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    quote: str
    start_char: int
    end_char: int


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent output models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class PaperInsight(BaseModel):
    """Extractor output. The four graded fields are all Optional by design:
    SPEC §14.2 forbids fabrication, so an unresolvable field is ``None`` plus an
    ``extraction_note``, never an invented string."""

    paper_id: str
    methodology: Optional[str] = None
    advantages: Optional[str] = None
    disadvantages: Optional[str] = None
    critique: Optional[str] = None
    datasets: list[str] = []
    metrics: list[str] = []
    results: Optional[str] = None
    limitations: Optional[str] = None
    cluster: Optional[str] = None  # C1..C6, SPEC §1.6
    evidence_spans: list[EvidenceSpan] = []
    extraction_note: Optional[str] = None


class Claim(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    text: str
    paper_ids: list[str]
    verdict: Verdict
    support_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    evidence: list[EvidenceSpan] = []


class SubQuestion(BaseModel):
    sq_id: str
    text: str
    facet: str  # method | application | evaluation | limitation
    covered: bool = False
    supporting_paper_ids: list[str] = []


class SearchTask(BaseModel):
    sq_id: str
    query: str
    sources: list[str]
    year_min: Optional[int] = None
    max_results: int = 25


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run configuration (types SPEC §10.1, revised for the $0 / CPU constraints)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class LLMConfig(BaseModel):
    """Generative-agent settings. Model names are checked against
    ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` here so a forbidden model fails at config load, not at
    the first billable request."""

    model: str
    planner_model: Optional[str] = None
    temperature: float = Field(default=0.1, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
    max_tokens: int = 4096
    requests_per_minute: int = 15
    max_retries: int = 5
    cache_dir: str = "data/llm_cache"

    @field_validator("model", "planner_model")
    @classmethod
    def _allowlisted(cls, v: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
        if v is not None and v not in ALLOWED_MODELS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Model {v!r} is not in ALLOWED_MODELS (TASKLIST §0.1: free, "
                f"open-weight models only). Permitted: {sorted(ALLOWED_MODELS)}"
            )
        return v


class EmbeddingsConfig(BaseModel):
    model: str = "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
    device: Literal["cpu", "cuda"] = "cpu"
    batch_size: int = 32


class RetrievalConfig(BaseModel):
    dense_k: int = 30
    sparse_k: int = 30
    fusion: Literal["rrf"] = "rrf"
    rrf_k: int = 60
    rerank: bool = True
    reranker: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2"
    final_k: int = 12
    chunk_size: int = 1200
    chunk_overlap: int = 200


class SourcesConfig(BaseModel):
    enabled: list[str] = ["openalex", "arxiv"]
    max_per_source: int = 25


class ReviewConfig(BaseModel):
    min_papers: int = 20

"""Core Pydantic data models.

Source of truth: RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §8. Every other module imports its shapes
from here; nothing in this file may import from the rest of the package, so it
stays dependency-free and safe to import anywhere.

Deviations from SPEC §8, all deliberate and recorded in TASKLIST.md:

* ``Paper.text_availability`` is new. TASKLIST T-204 sets it and T-505 enforces
  the abstract-only rule that depends on it (abstract-only papers may be cited
  as existing but may not supply verified claims).
* ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` lives here rather than in ``core/llm.py`` as TASKLIST §0.1
  originally said. Reason: this module has no dependencies, so ``core/config.py``
  can validate model names at config-load time instead of failing at the first
  API call. ``core/llm.py`` still owns *enforcement* — it imports and checks this
  constant before constructing any request.
* ``RunConfig`` and its nested models are new. SPEC §10.1 specifies the YAML but
  never types it, and SPEC's version predates the $0 constraint.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enumerations (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

VenueTier = Literal[
    "scopus_q1", "scopus", "ieee", "acl", "peer_reviewed", "preprint", "unknown"
]
Verdict = Literal["SUPPORTED", "PARTIAL", "UNSUPPORTED", "CONTRADICTED"]
Decision = Literal["WRITE", "RETRIEVE", "REPLAN"]
TextAvailability = Literal["full", "abstract_only", "none"]

#: TASKLIST §0.1 — the $0 hard rule. Only free, open-weight models.
#: Verified live 2026-08-25. ``core/llm.py`` raises on anything not in here.
ALLOWED_MODELS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        # Google AI Studio — open-weight Gemma, free tier
        "gemma-4-31b-it",
        "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
        # Groq — open-weight, free tier
        "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
        "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
        "qwen/qwen3.6-27b",
    }
)

#: Literature sources that actually have a connector in ``tools/search_sources.py``.
#: ``SourcesConfig`` validates against this so a config can never name a source
#: that does not exist — the failure mode that hid T-214 for a day, when
#: ``configs/default.yaml`` listed ``semantic_scholar`` and nothing implemented it.
IMPLEMENTED_SOURCES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {"openalex", "arxiv", "semantic_scholar"}
)

#: Provider inferred from model name; used by ``core/llm.py`` to pick a client.
MODEL_PROVIDER: dict[str, str] = {
    "gemma-4-31b-it": "google",
    "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it": "google",
    "openai/gpt-oss-120b": "groq",
    "openai/gpt-oss-20b": "groq",
    "qwen/qwen3.6-27b": "groq",
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corpus models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Paper(BaseModel):
    paper_id: str
    doi: Optional[str] = None
    title: str
    authors: list[str] = []
    year: Optional[int] = None
    venue: Optional[str] = None
    venue_tier: VenueTier = "unknown"
    abstract: Optional[str] = None
    url: Optional[str] = None
    pdf_path: Optional[str] = None
    source: str  # openalex | arxiv
    citation_count: Optional[int] = None
    is_preprint: bool = False
    #: Set by the PDF loader (T-204). Gates claim sourcing under T-505.
    text_availability: TextAvailability = "none"


class Chunk(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    paper_id: str
    text: str
    section: Optional[str] = None  # abstract | methods | results | ...
    start_char: int
    end_char: int
    embedding_id: Optional[str] = None

    @field_validator("end_char")
    @classmethod
    def _end_after_start(cls, v: int, info) -> int:
        start = info.data.get("start_char")
        if start is not None and v < start:
            raise ValueError(f"end_char {v} precedes start_char {start}")
        return v


class EvidenceSpan(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    quote: str
    start_char: int
    end_char: int


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent output models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class PaperInsight(BaseModel):
    """Extractor output. The four graded fields are all Optional by design:
    SPEC §14.2 forbids fabrication, so an unresolvable field is ``None`` plus an
    ``extraction_note``, never an invented string."""

    paper_id: str
    methodology: Optional[str] = None
    advantages: Optional[str] = None
    disadvantages: Optional[str] = None
    critique: Optional[str] = None
    datasets: list[str] = []
    metrics: list[str] = []
    results: Optional[str] = None
    limitations: Optional[str] = None
    cluster: Optional[str] = None  # C1..C6, SPEC §1.6
    evidence_spans: list[EvidenceSpan] = []
    extraction_note: Optional[str] = None


class Claim(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    text: str
    paper_ids: list[str]
    verdict: Verdict
    support_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    evidence: list[EvidenceSpan] = []


class SubQuestion(BaseModel):
    sq_id: str
    text: str
    facet: str  # method | application | evaluation | limitation
    covered: bool = False
    supporting_paper_ids: list[str] = []


class SearchTask(BaseModel):
    sq_id: str
    query: str
    sources: list[str]
    year_min: Optional[int] = None
    max_results: int = 25


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run configuration (types SPEC §10.1, revised for the $0 / CPU constraints)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class LLMConfig(BaseModel):
    """Generative-agent settings. Model names are checked against
    ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` here so a forbidden model fails at config load, not at
    the first billable request."""

    model: str

    def _allowlisted(cls, v: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:

                f"Model {v!r} is not in ALLOWED_MODELS (TASKLIST §0.1: free, "
                f"open-weight models only). Permitted: {sorted(ALLOWED_MODELS)}"

class RetrievalConfig(BaseModel):
    dense_k: int = 30
    sparse_k: int = 30
    fusion: Literal["rrf"] = "rrf"
    rrf_k: int = 60
    rerank: bool = True
    reranker: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2"
    final_k: int = 12
    chunk_size: int = 1200
    chunk_overlap: int = 200


class SourcesConfig(BaseModel):
    enabled: list[str] = ["openalex", "arxiv"]
    max_per_source: int = 25


class ReviewConfig(BaseModel):
    min_papers: int = 20
    max_papers: int = 60
    year_min: int = 2019
    max_iterations: int = 3
    grounding_threshold: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    coverage_threshold: float = Field(default=0.8, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


class VerifierConfig(BaseModel):
    onnx_path: str = "data/models/verifier-int8.onnx"
    tokenizer: str = "microsoft/deberta-v3-small"
    #: T-503 — biased toward precision. CliVER measured a 21% false-Support
    #: rate, and over-predicting "supported" is the dangerous direction here.
    support_threshold: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


class OutputConfig(BaseModel):
    citation_style: Literal["ieee"] = "ieee"
    formats: list[str] = ["markdown", "csv", "bibtex"]
    runs_dir: str = "outputs/runs"


class RunConfig(BaseModel):
    llm: LLMConfig
    embeddings: EmbeddingsConfig = EmbeddingsConfig()
    retrieval: RetrievalConfig = RetrievalConfig()
    sources: SourcesConfig = SourcesConfig()
    review: ReviewConfig = ReviewConfig()
    verifier: VerifierConfig = VerifierConfig()
    output: OutputConfig = OutputConfig()

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}

# SPEC §8 naming is canonical; these exist so both vocabularies resolve.

input.content:
"""T-213 diagnostic — why the gold papers T-212 never retrieved were missed.

T-212 (2026-08-26, ranked) found 13 of 35 gold papers anywhere in a 498-paper
union. Ranking cannot fix that: 0.371 is a hard ceiling on Recall@60 no matter
how good the reranker is. So the question that decides where the T-213 buffer
goes is not "how do we rank better" but:

    Are the 22 missing papers UNREACHABLE from our sources, or merely UNASKED
    for by the 15 hand-written stand-in queries?

Those have opposite fixes. Unreachable means the source set or the date window
is wrong — expensive. Unasked-for means query generation is wrong, which is the
Planner's job (T-402) and costs nothing extra to fix.

This probes each missed DOI three ways against OpenAlex:

  exact_title  - the full title as a search string. Reachable at all?
  doi_lookup   - direct /works/doi/... . In the index at all, window aside?
  short_query  - the first 4 content words, i.e. the shape our stand-in queries
                 use. Reachable by a query a Planner might plausibly emit?

The gap between ``exact_title`` and ``short_query`` is the size of the prize
sitting in T-402.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.diagnose_misses
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import time
from typing import Any

import httpx

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval import norm, norm_title
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import search_openalex

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
RESULT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/diagnose_misses_t213.json")

_STOP = {
    "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "by", "can", "for", "from", "in",
    "is", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "via", "with", "towards", "toward",
}


def short_query(title: str, n: int = 4) -> str:
    """The query shape our stand-in queries use: a few content words."""
    words = [w.strip(":,.—-") for w in title.lower().split()]
    content = [w for w in words if w and w not in _STOP]
    return " ".join(content[:n])


def doi_in_openalex(doi: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    url = f"https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/{doi}"
    try:
        with httpx.Client(timeout=30.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:
            resp = client.get(url, params={"mailto": "sreekaran005@gmail.com"})
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            return None
        return resp.json()
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        return None


def main() -> None:
    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    year_min = cfg.review.year_min

    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    by_doi = {norm(p["doi"]): p for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    missed = json.loads(RESULT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["missed"]

    print(f"diagnosing {len(missed)} never-retrieved gold papers "
          f"(year_min={year_min})\n")

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    tally = {"exact_title": 0, "doi_lookup": 0, "short_query": 0, "out_of_window": 0}

    for i, doi in enumerate(missed, 1):
        paper = by_doi.get(doi, {})
        title = paper.get("title") or ""
        want = norm_title(title)
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"doi": doi, "title": title, "year": paper.get("year")}

        record = doi_in_openalex(doi)
        row["doi_lookup"] = record is not None
        if record is not None:
            tally["doi_lookup"] += 1
            row["openalex_year"] = record.get("publication_year")
            if (record.get("publication_year") or 0) < year_min:
                row["out_of_window"] = True
                tally["out_of_window"] += 1

        try:
            hits = search_openalex(title[:180], year_min=year_min, max_results=10)
        except Exception:
            hits = []
        row["exact_title"] = any(
            norm(h.doi) == doi or norm_title(h.title) == want for h in hits
        )
        tally["exact_title"] += bool(row["exact_title"])

        sq = short_query(title)
        row["short_query_text"] = sq
        try:
            hits = search_openalex(sq, year_min=year_min, max_results=25)
        except Exception:
            hits = []
        row["short_query"] = any(
            norm(h.doi) == doi or norm_title(h.title) == want for h in hits
        )
        tally["short_query"] += bool(row["short_query"])

        flag = (
            "UNASKED " if row["exact_title"] and not row["short_query"]
            else "reachable" if row["short_query"]
            else "UNREACHABLE"
        )
        print(f"  [{i:2d}/{len(missed)}] {flag}  {title[:56]}")
        rows.append(row)
        time.sleep(0.4)  # be polite to OpenAlex

    n = len(missed) or 1
    print("\n" + "=" * 66)
    print(f"in OpenAlex at all (DOI lookup)   {tally['doi_lookup']:2d}/{n}")
    print(f"  of those, published < {year_min}      {tally['out_of_window']:2d}  "
          f"(excluded by our own date window)")
    print(f"findable by EXACT TITLE           {tally['exact_title']:2d}/{n}")
    print(f"findable by a SHORT QUERY         {tally['short_query']:2d}/{n}")
    prize = tally["exact_title"] - tally["short_query"]
    print("=" * 66)
    print(f"\nreachable but not asked for: {prize}/{n} papers.")
    print("These need better QUERIES (T-402), not a better index or model.")
    unreachable = n - tally["exact_title"]
    print(f"genuinely unreachable from OpenAlex: {unreachable}/{n}.")

    OUT.write_text(
        json.dumps({"year_min": year_min, "tally": tally, "papers": rows}, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text: The confound is in my ranking stage: `dense_k`/`sparse_k` are fixed at 30, so the first stage is a **global** top-60 over the whole pool. At pool=1962 that discards most of each sub-question's own candidates before the reranker ever sees them — so pool size itself changes the measurement. Fixing that, plus caching so sweeps stop costing 18 minutes of Semantic Scholar backoff:

chunks = [as_chunk(k, p) for k, p in pool.items()]
    print(f"\nranking {len(chunks)} pooled papers through T-209 + T-210 ...", flush=True)

    # ⚠️ The first stage must not be narrower than what one sub-question
    # retrieved live. With the production dense_k/sparse_k of 30, ``retrieve()``
    # returns a *global* top-60 over the whole pool; intersecting that with one
    # sub-question's own candidates then throws most of them away, and throws
    # away more of them the larger the pool gets. That makes pool size itself
    # change the score — measured 2026-08-26: raising max_per_source 25 -> 100
    # nearly doubled union recall (0.371 -> 0.714) while the Recall@60 gate
    # *fell* (0.057 -> 0.029), which is an artefact of this narrowing, not a
    # property of retrieval. Widening the first stage to the whole pool removes
    # the confound: RRF still fuses dense + sparse exactly as T-209 specifies,
    # it just no longer truncates before the reranker sees the candidates.
    rank_cfg = cfg.retrieval.model_copy(
        update={"dense_k": len(chunks), "sparse_k": len(chunks)}
    )

    embedder = Embedder(
        model_name=cfg.embeddings.model,
        device=cfg.embeddings.device,
        batch_size=cfg.embeddings.batch_size,
    )
    embeddings = embedder.encode([c.text for c in chunks])

    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True) as tmp:
        store = VectorStore(path=tmp, collection="t212")
        store.add(chunks, embeddings)
        bm25 = BM25Index()
        bm25.build(chunks)
        retriever = HybridRetriever(store, bm25, embedder, rank_cfg)

cd "C:/Users/Sreekaran/Desktop/Major Project" && python - <<'EOF'
import pathlib
p = pathlib.Path("tests/test_phase2_acceptance.py")
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

TEST = '''

def test_t213_first_stage_survives_a_large_pool() -> None:
    """T-213(2) regression: pool size must not change what gets ranked.

    ``HybridRetriever`` is configured with dense_k/sparse_k = 30 in production.
    The T-212 harness ranks a pool of up to ~2000 pooled papers, so a fixed
    top-60 first stage returns a *global* shortlist; intersecting that with one
    sub-question's own candidates discards more of them the bigger the pool
    gets. Measured 2026-08-26: raising max_per_source 25 -> 100 nearly doubled
    union recall (0.371 -> 0.714) while the Recall@60 gate *fell*
    (0.057 -> 0.029) — an artefact of this narrowing, not of retrieval.

    Fails if the first stage is ever narrowed back below the pool size.
    """
    from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
    from researchgpt.eval import retrieval_eval as ev

    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    n_pool, n_per_query = 220, 45
    assert n_per_query > cfg.retrieval.dense_k, "pool must exceed the production first stage"

    pool = {
        f"p{i}": Paper(
            paper_id=f"p{i}",
            doi=f"10.1234/p{i}",
            title=f"Paper {i} on retrieval augmented generation and agents",
            abstract=f"Study number {i} of hybrid retrieval, reranking and citation grounding.",
            source="openalex",
        )
        for i in range(n_pool)
    }
    queries = ["hybrid retrieval reranking", "citation grounding agents"]
    per_query = {
        queries[0]: [f"p{i}" for i in range(n_per_query)],
        queries[1]: [f"p{i}" for i in range(n_per_query, 2 * n_per_query)],
    }
    expected = {k for keys in per_query.values() for k in keys}

    original = ev.QUERIES
    ev.QUERIES = queries
    try:
        ordered = ev.rank_corpus(per_query, pool, cfg)
    finally:
        ev.QUERIES = original

    assert len(ordered) == n_pool, "every pooled paper must still appear"
    assert len(set(ordered)) == n_pool, "ranking must not duplicate"
    head = set(ordered[: len(expected)])
    missing = expected - head
    assert not missing, (
        f"{len(missing)} of {len(expected)} live candidates were dropped by the "
        f"first stage before the reranker saw them — the pool-size confound is back"
    )
    print(f"T-213 first-stage OK ({len(expected)} candidates ranked from a {n_pool} pool)")

'''

"""T-213 diagnostic — why the gold papers T-212 never retrieved were missed.

T-212 (2026-08-26, ranked) found 13 of 35 gold papers anywhere in a 498-paper
union. Ranking cannot fix that: 0.371 is a hard ceiling on Recall@60 no matter
how good the reranker is. So the question that decides where the T-213 buffer
goes is not "how do we rank better" but:

    Are the 22 missing papers UNREACHABLE from our sources, or merely UNASKED
    for by the 15 hand-written stand-in queries?

Those have opposite fixes. Unreachable means the source set or the date window
is wrong — expensive. Unasked-for means query generation is wrong, which is the
Planner's job (T-402) and costs nothing extra to fix.

This probes each missed DOI three ways against OpenAlex:

  exact_title  - the full title as a search string. Reachable at all?
  doi_lookup   - direct /works/doi/... . In the index at all, window aside?
  short_query  - the first 4 content words, i.e. the shape our stand-in queries
                 use. Reachable by a query a Planner might plausibly emit?

The gap between ``exact_title`` and ``short_query`` is the size of the prize
sitting in T-402.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.diagnose_misses
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import time
from typing import Any

import httpx

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval import norm, norm_title
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import search_openalex

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
RESULT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/diagnose_misses_t213.json")

_STOP = {
    "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "by", "can", "for", "from", "in",
    "is", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "via", "with", "towards", "toward",
}


def short_query(title: str, n: int = 4) -> str:
    """The query shape our stand-in queries use: a few content words."""
    words = [w.strip(":,.—-") for w in title.lower().split()]
    content = [w for w in words if w and w not in _STOP]
    return " ".join(content[:n])


def doi_in_openalex(doi: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    url = f"https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/{doi}"
    try:
        with httpx.Client(timeout=30.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:
            resp = client.get(url, params={"mailto": "sreekaran005@gmail.com"})
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            return None
        return resp.json()
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        return None


def main() -> None:
    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    year_min = cfg.review.year_min

    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    by_doi = {norm(p["doi"]): p for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    missed = json.loads(RESULT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["missed"]

    print(f"diagnosing {len(missed)} never-retrieved gold papers "
          f"(year_min={year_min})\n")

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    tally = {"exact_title": 0, "doi_lookup": 0, "short_query": 0, "out_of_window": 0}

    for i, doi in enumerate(missed, 1):
        paper = by_doi.get(doi, {})
        title = paper.get("title") or ""
        want = norm_title(title)
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"doi": doi, "title": title, "year": paper.get("year")}

        record = doi_in_openalex(doi)
        row["doi_lookup"] = record is not None
        if record is not None:
            tally["doi_lookup"] += 1
            row["openalex_year"] = record.get("publication_year")
            if (record.get("publication_year") or 0) < year_min:
                row["out_of_window"] = True
                tally["out_of_window"] += 1

        try:
            hits = search_openalex(title[:180], year_min=year_min, max_results=10)
        except Exception:
            hits = []
        row["exact_title"] = any(
            norm(h.doi) == doi or norm_title(h.title) == want for h in hits
        )
        tally["exact_title"] += bool(row["exact_title"])

        sq = short_query(title)
        row["short_query_text"] = sq
        try:
            hits = search_openalex(sq, year_min=year_min, max_results=25)
        except Exception:
            hits = []
        row["short_query"] = any(
            norm(h.doi) == doi or norm_title(h.title) == want for h in hits
        )
        tally["short_query"] += bool(row["short_query"])

        flag = (
            "UNASKED " if row["exact_title"] and not row["short_query"]
            else "reachable" if row["short_query"]
            else "UNREACHABLE"
        )
        print(f"  [{i:2d}/{len(missed)}] {flag}  {title[:56]}")
        rows.append(row)
        time.sleep(0.4)  # be polite to OpenAlex

    n = len(missed) or 1
    print("\n" + "=" * 66)
    print(f"in OpenAlex at all (DOI lookup)   {tally['doi_lookup']:2d}/{n}")
    print(f"  of those, published < {year_min}      {tally['out_of_window']:2d}  "
          f"(excluded by our own date window)")
    print(f"findable by EXACT TITLE           {tally['exact_title']:2d}/{n}")
    print(f"findable by a SHORT QUERY         {tally['short_query']:2d}/{n}")
    prize = tally["exact_title"] - tally["short_query"]
    print("=" * 66)
    print(f"\nreachable but not asked for: {prize}/{n} papers.")
    print("These need better QUERIES (T-402), not a better index or model.")
    unreachable = n - tally["exact_title"]
    print(f"genuinely unreachable from OpenAlex: {unreachable}/{n}.")

    OUT.write_text(
        json.dumps({"year_min": year_min, "tally": tally, "papers": rows}, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

## T-214 — Semantic Scholar connector ✅

Built test-first in `tools/search_sources.py`. Five acceptance tests, all green:

- **Mapping** — every field per the handoff, against a captured payload: DOI URL → bare lowercase via T-201's `normalise_doi`, empty-string venue → `None`, `is_preprint = "JournalArticle" not in publicationTypes`, plain-text abstracts.

- **Live** — 20 papers, 14 abstracts, 19 normalised DOIs.

**Evidence for T-215 (yours to do):** across live runs, Semantic Scholar throttled out on roughly **2 of every 3 queries** keyless, each burning the full 60s backoff. It degrades correctly every time, but it contributes about a third of the time. Worth applying for the free academic key.

| run | pool | union recall | **Recall@60** |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-25 unranked | 447 | 0.371 | 0.029 |
| `mps=25` ranked | 493 | 0.371 | **0.057** |

**Two of my own hypotheses were refuted by the data**, and I've recorded both in the TASKLIST so they don't get retried:

1. I told you DOI-only matching was undercounting because arXiv preprints carry synthetic DOIs. Title-fallback matching adds **exactly 0.000** at `mps=25`. I verified the metric isn't dead — a synthetic preprint-of-a-gold-paper scores and doesn't double-count — so the misses are genuine absences. I was wrong.
2. I then assumed the `mps=100` drop was an artefact of my narrow first stage. Fixing it changed the gate by **nothing**, even though the first stage now keeps 100–217 candidates per sub-question instead of ~30. The drop is real.

**The binding constraint is query generation** — confirmed three ways:
- Of the 10 papers never retrieved, **10/10 are in OpenAlex**, **0** excluded by the date window, and **9/10 are findable by exactly the short-query shape we already use**. They weren't unreachable; they were never asked for.
- Pooled gold papers rank 38 times across the 15 sub-questions, but only **2 reach rank ≤4** — and ≤4 is all a 60-paper corpus over 15 sub-questions can take.
- The stock reranker is **above chance but barely** (2 top-4 hits vs 1.19 expected at random). Where a query was specific, gold landed at ranks **1 and 2**.

## Three decisions for you

- **Don't adopt `max_per_source: 100`.** It nearly doubles the ceiling but makes the corpus the Extractor actually sees *worse* (2 gold in top-60 → 1). I left `configs/default.yaml` unchanged.

- `SourcesConfig.enabled` now validates against `IMPLEMENTED_SOURCES` — the guard that would have caught T-214's absence, since the config named a connector nothing implemented and nothing checked.
- A **dead assertion** in T-202's test: it referenced an undefined name inside a short-circuited generator, so it never executed.
- `load_dotenv()` in `Embedder`/`Reranker` — the open HF-token item from `handoffs/phase2_complete.md §4.4`.

"""T-213 diagnostic — why the gold papers T-212 never retrieved were missed.

T-212 (2026-08-26, ranked) found 13 of 35 gold papers anywhere in a 498-paper
union. Ranking cannot fix that: 0.371 is a hard ceiling on Recall@60 no matter
how good the reranker is. So the question that decides where the T-213 buffer
goes is not "how do we rank better" but:

    Are the 22 missing papers UNREACHABLE from our sources, or merely UNASKED
    for by the 15 hand-written stand-in queries?

Those have opposite fixes. Unreachable means the source set or the date window
is wrong — expensive. Unasked-for means query generation is wrong, which is the
Planner's job (T-402) and costs nothing extra to fix.

This probes each missed DOI three ways against OpenAlex:

  exact_title  - the full title as a search string. Reachable at all?
  doi_lookup   - direct /works/doi/... . In the index at all, window aside?
  short_query  - the first 4 content words, i.e. the shape our stand-in queries
                 use. Reachable by a query a Planner might plausibly emit?

The gap between ``exact_title`` and ``short_query`` is the size of the prize
sitting in T-402.

Run:  python -m researchgpt.eval.diagnose_misses
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import time
from typing import Any

import httpx

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval import norm, norm_title
from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import search_openalex

GOLD = pathlib.Path("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json")
RESULT = pathlib.Path("eval/retrieval_eval_t212.json")
OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/diagnose_misses_t213.json")

_STOP = {
    "a", "an", "and", "are", "as", "at", "be", "by", "can", "for", "from", "in",
    "is", "of", "on", "or", "the", "to", "via", "with", "towards", "toward",
}


def short_query(title: str, n: int = 4) -> str:
    """The query shape our stand-in queries use: a few content words."""
    words = [w.strip(":,.—-") for w in title.lower().split()]
    content = [w for w in words if w and w not in _STOP]
    return " ".join(content[:n])


def doi_in_openalex(doi: str) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    url = f"https://api.openalex.org/works/https://doi.org/{doi}"
    try:
        with httpx.Client(timeout=30.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:
            resp = client.get(url, params={"mailto": "sreekaran005@gmail.com"})
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            return None
        return resp.json()
    except httpx.HTTPError:
        return None


def main() -> None:
    cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
    year_min = cfg.review.year_min

    gold_doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    by_doi = {norm(p["doi"]): p for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
    missed = json.loads(RESULT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["missed"]

    print(f"diagnosing {len(missed)} never-retrieved gold papers "
          f"(year_min={year_min})\n")

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    tally = {"exact_title": 0, "doi_lookup": 0, "short_query": 0, "out_of_window": 0}

    for i, doi in enumerate(missed, 1):
        paper = by_doi.get(doi, {})
        title = paper.get("title") or ""
        want = norm_title(title)
        row: dict[str, Any] = {"doi": doi, "title": title, "year": paper.get("year")}

        record = doi_in_openalex(doi)
        row["doi_lookup"] = record is not None
        if record is not None:
            tally["doi_lookup"] += 1
            row["openalex_year"] = record.get("publication_year")
            if (record.get("publication_year") or 0) < year_min:
                row["out_of_window"] = True
                tally["out_of_window"] += 1

        try:
            hits = search_openalex(title[:180], year_min=year_min, max_results=10)
        except Exception:
            hits = []
        row["exact_title"] = any(
            norm(h.doi) == doi or norm_title(h.title) == want for h in hits
        )
        tally["exact_title"] += bool(row["exact_title"])

        sq = short_query(title)
        row["short_query_text"] = sq
        try:
            hits = search_openalex(sq, year_min=year_min, max_results=25)
        except Exception:
            hits = []
        row["short_query"] = any(
            norm(h.doi) == doi or norm_title(h.title) == want for h in hits
        )
        tally["short_query"] += bool(row["short_query"])

        flag = (
            "UNASKED " if row["exact_title"] and not row["short_query"]
            else "reachable" if row["short_query"]
            else "UNREACHABLE"
        )
        print(f"  [{i:2d}/{len(missed)}] {flag}  {title[:56]}")
        rows.append(row)
        time.sleep(0.4)  # be polite to OpenAlex

    n = len(missed) or 1
    print("\n" + "=" * 66)
    print(f"in OpenAlex at all (DOI lookup)   {tally['doi_lookup']:2d}/{n}")
    print(f"  of those, published < {year_min}      {tally['out_of_window']:2d}  "
          f"(excluded by our own date window)")
    print(f"findable by EXACT TITLE           {tally['exact_title']:2d}/{n}")
    print(f"findable by a SHORT QUERY         {tally['short_query']:2d}/{n}")
    print("=" * 66)
    # Reachable = findable by EITHER probe. A short query sometimes beats the
    # exact-title probe, because the title search is truncated to 180 chars and
    # OpenAlex ANDs every term in it — so the two are a union, not a hierarchy.
    reachable = sum(1 for r in rows if r["exact_title"] or r["short_query"])
    print(f"\nreachable by some query, but our 15 never asked: {reachable}/{n}.")
    print("These need better QUERIES (T-402), not a better index or model.")
    print(f"genuinely unreachable from OpenAlex search: {n - reachable}/{n}.")

    OUT.write_text(
        json.dumps({"year_min": year_min, "tally": tally, "papers": rows}, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"\nwrote {OUT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Where do the in-pool gold papers actually rank? Uses the cached pool, no network."""
import io
import json
import pathlib
import tempfile

from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.core.models import Paper
from researchgpt.data.bm25_index import BM25Index
from researchgpt.data.embeddings import Embedder
from researchgpt.data.vectorstore import VectorStore
from researchgpt.eval.retrieval_eval import as_chunk, norm, norm_title
from researchgpt.tools.hybrid_retriever import HybridRetriever
from researchgpt.tools.reranker import Reranker

MPS = 100
cache = json.loads(pathlib.Path(f"eval/cache/pool_mps{MPS}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
pool = {k: Paper(**v) for k, v in cache["pool"].items()}
per_query = cache["per_query"]

gold_doc = json.load(io.open("eval/gold_sets/own_bibliography.json", encoding="utf-8"))
gold_dois = {norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("doi")}
gold_titles = {norm_title(p["title"]): norm(p["doi"]) for p in gold_doc["papers"] if p.get("title")}


def is_gold(p):
    d, t = norm(p.doi), norm_title(p.title)
    if d and d in gold_dois:
        return d
    if t and t in gold_titles:
        return gold_titles[t]
    return None


cfg = load_config("configs/default.yaml")
chunks = [as_chunk(k, p) for k, p in pool.items()]
in_pool = {k: g for k, p in pool.items() if (g := is_gold(p))}
print(f"pool={len(chunks)}  gold present in pool={len(set(in_pool.values()))}\n")

rank_cfg = cfg.retrieval.model_copy(update={"dense_k": len(chunks), "sparse_k": len(chunks)})
emb = Embedder(model_name=cfg.embeddings.model, device="cpu", batch_size=cfg.embeddings.batch_size)
vecs = emb.encode([c.text for c in chunks])

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(ignore_cleanup_errors=True) as tmp:
    store = VectorStore(path=tmp, collection="diag")
    store.add(chunks, vecs)
    bm25 = BM25Index()
    bm25.build(chunks)
    retr = HybridRetriever(store, bm25, emb, rank_cfg)
    rr = Reranker(model_name=cfg.retrieval.reranker, device="cpu")

    print(f"{'query':46s} {'cands':>6s} {'gold':>5s} {'ranks of gold (1-based)'}")
    print("-" * 100)
    all_ranks = []
    for q, keys in per_query.items():
        allowed = set(keys)
        fused = retr.retrieve(q)
        cands = [c for c, _ in fused if c.chunk_id in allowed]
        if not cands:
            continue
        top = rr.rerank(q, cands, top_k=len(cands))
        order = [c.chunk_id for c, _ in top]
        ranks = [i + 1 for i, k in enumerate(order) if k in in_pool]
        all_ranks += [(r, len(order)) for r in ranks]
        shown = ranks[:8]
        print(f"{q[:46]:46s} {len(cands):6d} {len(ranks):5d} {shown}")
    store.reset()

print("\n" + "=" * 70)
top4 = sum(1 for r, _ in all_ranks if r <= 4)
top10 = sum(1 for r, _ in all_ranks if r <= 10)
print(f"gold appearances across all sub-question rankings: {len(all_ranks)}")
print(f"  reaching rank <= 4  (what a 60-paper round-robin takes): {top4}")
print(f"  reaching rank <= 10:                                     {top10}")
if all_ranks:
    exp = sum(4 / n for _, n in all_ranks)
    print(f"\nexpected top-4 hits if ranking were RANDOM: {exp:.2f}")
    print(f"actual top-4 hits:                          {top4}")
    print("=> reranker is ADDING signal" if top4 > exp * 1.5 else "=> reranker is at/near CHANCE")

"""Core Pydantic data models.

Source of truth: RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md §8. Every other module imports its shapes
from here; nothing in this file may import from the rest of the package, so it
stays dependency-free and safe to import anywhere.

Deviations from SPEC §8, all deliberate and recorded in TASKLIST.md:

* ``Paper.text_availability`` is new. TASKLIST T-204 sets it and T-505 enforces
  the abstract-only rule that depends on it (abstract-only papers may be cited
  as existing but may not supply verified claims).
* ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` lives here rather than in ``core/llm.py`` as TASKLIST §0.1
  originally said. Reason: this module has no dependencies, so ``core/config.py``
  can validate model names at config-load time instead of failing at the first
  API call. ``core/llm.py`` still owns *enforcement* — it imports and checks this
  constant before constructing any request.
* ``RunConfig`` and its nested models are new. SPEC §10.1 specifies the YAML but
  never types it, and SPEC's version predates the $0 constraint.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Literal, Optional

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Enumerations (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

VenueTier = Literal[
    "scopus_q1", "scopus", "ieee", "acl", "peer_reviewed", "preprint", "unknown"
]
Verdict = Literal["SUPPORTED", "PARTIAL", "UNSUPPORTED", "CONTRADICTED"]
Decision = Literal["WRITE", "RETRIEVE", "REPLAN"]
TextAvailability = Literal["full", "abstract_only", "none"]

#: TASKLIST §0.1 — the $0 hard rule. Only free, open-weight models.
#: Verified live 2026-08-25. ``core/llm.py`` raises on anything not in here.
ALLOWED_MODELS: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {
        # Google AI Studio — open-weight Gemma, free tier
        "gemma-4-31b-it",
        "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it",
        # Groq — open-weight, free tier
        "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
        "openai/gpt-oss-20b",
        "qwen/qwen3.6-27b",
    }
)

#: Literature sources that actually have a connector in ``tools/search_sources.py``.
#: ``SourcesConfig`` validates against this so a config can never name a source
#: that does not exist — the failure mode that hid T-214 for a day, when
#: ``configs/default.yaml`` listed ``semantic_scholar`` and nothing implemented it.
IMPLEMENTED_SOURCES: frozenset[str] = frozenset(
    {"openalex", "arxiv", "semantic_scholar"}
)

#: Provider inferred from model name; used by ``core/llm.py`` to pick a client.
MODEL_PROVIDER: dict[str, str] = {
    "gemma-4-31b-it": "google",
    "gemma-4-26b-a4b-it": "google",
    "openai/gpt-oss-120b": "groq",
    "openai/gpt-oss-20b": "groq",
    "qwen/qwen3.6-27b": "groq",
}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Corpus models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Paper(BaseModel):
    paper_id: str
    doi: Optional[str] = None
    title: str
    authors: list[str] = []
    year: Optional[int] = None
    venue: Optional[str] = None
    venue_tier: VenueTier = "unknown"
    abstract: Optional[str] = None
    url: Optional[str] = None
    pdf_path: Optional[str] = None
    source: str  # openalex | arxiv
    citation_count: Optional[int] = None
    is_preprint: bool = False
    #: Set by the PDF loader (T-204). Gates claim sourcing under T-505.
    text_availability: TextAvailability = "none"


class Chunk(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    paper_id: str
    text: str
    section: Optional[str] = None  # abstract | methods | results | ...
    start_char: int
    end_char: int
    embedding_id: Optional[str] = None

    @field_validator("end_char")
    @classmethod
    def _end_after_start(cls, v: int, info) -> int:
        start = info.data.get("start_char")
        if start is not None and v < start:
            raise ValueError(f"end_char {v} precedes start_char {start}")
        return v


class EvidenceSpan(BaseModel):
    chunk_id: str
    quote: str
    start_char: int
    end_char: int


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent output models (SPEC §8)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class PaperInsight(BaseModel):
    """Extractor output. The four graded fields are all Optional by design:
    SPEC §14.2 forbids fabrication, so an unresolvable field is ``None`` plus an
    ``extraction_note``, never an invented string."""

    paper_id: str
    methodology: Optional[str] = None
    advantages: Optional[str] = None
    disadvantages: Optional[str] = None
    critique: Optional[str] = None
    datasets: list[str] = []
    metrics: list[str] = []
    results: Optional[str] = None
    limitations: Optional[str] = None
    cluster: Optional[str] = None  # C1..C6, SPEC §1.6
    evidence_spans: list[EvidenceSpan] = []
    extraction_note: Optional[str] = None


class Claim(BaseModel):
    claim_id: str
    text: str
    paper_ids: list[str]
    verdict: Verdict
    support_score: float = Field(ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    evidence: list[EvidenceSpan] = []


class SubQuestion(BaseModel):
    sq_id: str
    text: str
    facet: str  # method | application | evaluation | limitation
    covered: bool = False
    supporting_paper_ids: list[str] = []


class SearchTask(BaseModel):
    sq_id: str
    query: str
    sources: list[str]
    year_min: Optional[int] = None
    max_results: int = 25


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Run configuration (types SPEC §10.1, revised for the $0 / CPU constraints)
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


class LLMConfig(BaseModel):
    """Generative-agent settings. Model names are checked against
    ``ALLOWED_MODELS`` here so a forbidden model fails at config load, not at
    the first billable request."""

    model: str
    planner_model: Optional[str] = None
    temperature: float = Field(default=0.1, ge=0.0, le=2.0)
    max_tokens: int = 4096
    requests_per_minute: int = 15
    max_retries: int = 5
    cache_dir: str = "data/llm_cache"

    @field_validator("model", "planner_model")
    @classmethod
    def _allowlisted(cls, v: Optional[str]) -> Optional[str]:
        if v is not None and v not in ALLOWED_MODELS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Model {v!r} is not in ALLOWED_MODELS (TASKLIST §0.1: free, "
                f"open-weight models only). Permitted: {sorted(ALLOWED_MODELS)}"
            )
        return v


class EmbeddingsConfig(BaseModel):
    model: str = "BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5"
    device: Literal["cpu", "cuda"] = "cpu"
    batch_size: int = 32


class RetrievalConfig(BaseModel):
    dense_k: int = 30
    sparse_k: int = 30
    fusion: Literal["rrf"] = "rrf"
    rrf_k: int = 60
    rerank: bool = True
    reranker: str = "cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2"
    final_k: int = 12
    chunk_size: int = 1200
    chunk_overlap: int = 200


class SourcesConfig(BaseModel):
    enabled: list[str] = ["openalex", "arxiv"]
    max_per_source: int = 25

    @field_validator("enabled")
    @classmethod
    def _implemented(cls, v: list[str]) -> list[str]:
        unknown = [s for s in v if s not in IMPLEMENTED_SOURCES]
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(
                f"sources.enabled names {unknown}, which have no connector in "
                f"tools/search_sources.py. Implemented: {sorted(IMPLEMENTED_SOURCES)}"
            )
        return v


class ReviewConfig(BaseModel):
    min_papers: int = 20
    max_papers: int = 60
    year_min: int = 2019
    max_iterations: int = 3
    grounding_threshold: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)
    coverage_threshold: float = Field(default=0.8, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


class VerifierConfig(BaseModel):
    onnx_path: str = "data/models/verifier-int8.onnx"
    tokenizer: str = "microsoft/deberta-v3-small"
    #: T-503 — biased toward precision. CliVER measured a 21% false-Support
    #: rate, and over-predicting "supported" is the dangerous direction here.
    support_threshold: float = Field(default=0.7, ge=0.0, le=1.0)


class OutputConfig(BaseModel):
    citation_style: Literal["ieee"] = "ieee"
    formats: list[str] = ["markdown", "csv", "bibtex"]
    runs_dir: str = "outputs/runs"


class RunConfig(BaseModel):
    llm: LLMConfig
    embeddings: EmbeddingsConfig = EmbeddingsConfig()
    retrieval: RetrievalConfig = RetrievalConfig()
    sources: SourcesConfig = SourcesConfig()
    review: ReviewConfig = ReviewConfig()
    verifier: VerifierConfig = VerifierConfig()
    output: OutputConfig = OutputConfig()

    model_config = {"extra": "forbid"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Aliases for the names used in TASKLIST T-102's acceptance criterion.
# SPEC §8 naming is canonical; these exist so both vocabularies resolve.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

Insight = PaperInsight
CritiqueDecision = Decision

__all__ = [
    "ALLOWED_MODELS",
    "IMPLEMENTED_SOURCES",
    "MODEL_PROVIDER",
    "VenueTier",
    "Verdict",
    "Decision",
    "CritiqueDecision",
    "TextAvailability",
    "Paper",
    "Chunk",
    "EvidenceSpan",
    "PaperInsight",
    "Insight",
    "Claim",
    "SubQuestion",
    "SearchTask",
    "LLMConfig",
    "EmbeddingsConfig",
    "RetrievalConfig",
    "SourcesConfig",
    "ReviewConfig",
    "VerifierConfig",
    "OutputConfig",
    "RunConfig",
]

- academic-research-skills:research_architect_agent: Designs the methodological blueprint; selects research paradigm, method, data strategy, and analytical framework (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Glob)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

# ResearchGPT — Master Task List

> **What this file is.** The single executable backlog for the whole project, derived from `PROJECT_PLAN.md`, `RESEARCHGPT_SPEC.md`, `SESSION_CONTEXT.md`, `ARCHITECTURE_REVIEW.md` and the two `diagrams/*_EXPLAINED.md` files.
>
> **Two-agent workflow.** **Claude Code plans, specifies, reviews and integrates. Cursor (Groq) writes the code.** Every task below is written so it can be handed to Cursor as a self-contained unit of work with a hard acceptance test.
>
> **Companion documents:** `TRAINING_SPEC.md` (both fine-tuned models — verifier and reranker — and why the generative agents are not trained), `DB_SCHEMA.md` (the Postgres run registry), `PROJECT_PLAN.md` (scope), `SESSION_CONTEXT.md` (constraints and literature findings).
>
> Created 2026-08-25. Update the checkboxes in place; do not rewrite the file.

---

## 0. Reality check — read this before anything else

| | |
|---|---|
| Plan written | 2026-08-06 (30-day plan, Day 1 = 2026-08-07) |
| Today | **2026-08-25** |
| Target submission | **~2026-09-07** (was ~09-05; +2 days authorised 2026-08-25 to integrate SciReviewGen) |
| Days actually remaining | **13** |
| Code written so far | **Zero.** No `src/`, no `pyproject.toml`, no `.py` file anywhere in the folder. |

**The 30-day plan is no longer executable as written.** Nineteen of its thirty days are gone and none of them produced code. What exists is planning, literature, design and two graded decks.

This file is therefore **not** the 30-day plan re-typed. It is a compressed 11-day plan that applies the descope ladder in `PROJECT_PLAN.md §10` **up front** rather than in a panic on Day 28. Concretely, the following are cut before starting, not deferred:

| Cut now | Was | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Ollama feasibility probe | §6.3 | Already demoted to a footnote. Dead. |
| DOCX writer | §2.2 | Markdown + PDF-from-Markdown suffices. |
| 2-annotator Likert + Cohen's κ | §9 | Scheduling cost exceeds its evidentiary value at 11 days. Replaced by the 50-claim spot-check. |
| Ablations 3 and 4 | §9.4 | Kept only if Phase 7 finishes early. **Ablation 2 is never cut.** |

================================================================================
Written 2026-08-27 by Claude Code, from a full pass over TASKLIST.md.
Target submission: ~2026-09-07.  Days remaining: 11.

      Highest grade ceiling. Also the option where M1 slips, and the Aug 31
      M1 deadline is the one TASKLIST calls "the insurance policy."

  (b) Keep 3B, drop 3C, drop 6B.  [RECOMMENDED]
