"""T-304 — export the trained verifier to ONNX + int8, and prove it still works.

The pipeline runs on CPU with no torch at inference time (``pyproject.toml``'s
``verify`` extra deliberately omits torch), so the Kaggle checkpoint has to
become an ONNX graph before ``agents/verifier.py`` can use it.

**The acceptance criterion is a parity check, not a successful export.** An
export that silently produces garbage still "succeeds". Two separate checks,
because they fail for different reasons:

``PyTorch -> ONNX fp32``  logits must agree to ~1e-3 **and** argmax 100%.
                          This is the *export correctness* test. Measured
                          2026-08-27 on the stock checkpoint: max |dlogit|
                          **8e-6**, argmax 20/20, and identical macro-F1 on the
                          full 628-pair held-out set (0.516 both ways).

``ONNX fp32 -> int8``     gated on **macro-F1 over the whole held-out set**,
                          not on per-pair argmax.

⚠️ **The int8 gate was originally per-pair argmax agreement on 20 examples, and
that was the wrong test.** Measured on the stock checkpoint, dynamic int8 flips
**2 of 20** individual decisions and moves single logits by up to 4.2 — which
looks alarming — yet over the full 628-pair set it costs *nothing*:

    ONNX fp32               accuracy 0.553   macro-F1 0.516
    int8 per_channel=False  accuracy 0.554   macro-F1 0.538
    int8 per_channel=True   accuracy 0.556   macro-F1 0.539

The flips go both ways and cancel. A 20-sample argmax gate would have rejected
a quantization that is demonstrably free, so the gate now measures the thing
that actually matters. DeBERTa's disentangled attention is genuinely
quantization-sensitive per-logit; it just does not matter in aggregate.

``per_channel=True`` is the default on that evidence — same size, marginally
better, no downside found.

Run::

    # after downloading and unzipping the Kaggle output
    python -m researchgpt.verify.export_onnx --checkpoint data/models/verifier-scifact

    # dry-run the whole path against the stock checkpoint, before Kaggle returns
    python -m researchgpt.verify.export_onnx --checkpoint cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-small
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import shutil
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import encode_pair
from researchgpt.verify.labels import LABELS
from researchgpt.verify.scifact_pairs import read_jsonl

DEFAULT_PAIRS = pathlib.Path("data/scifact/pairs_validation.jsonl")
DEFAULT_OUT = pathlib.Path("data/models/verifier-onnx")

#: ONNX fp32 must be a faithful re-encoding of the PyTorch graph.
FP32_TOLERANCE = 1e-3
#: int8 is lossy on purpose; this only catches a catastrophically bad calibration.
INT8_TOLERANCE = 2.0


def _tokenize(tokenizer: Any, pairs: list[dict[str, Any]], max_length: int, framework: str):
    return tokenizer(
        [encode_pair(p)[0] for p in pairs],
        [encode_pair(p)[1] for p in pairs],
        padding=True,
        truncation=True,
        max_length=max_length,
        return_tensors=framework,
    )


def export(
    checkpoint: str,
    out_dir: pathlib.Path,
    *,
    pairs: list[dict[str, Any]],
    max_length: int = 256,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Export, quantize, and parity-check. Returns the report dict."""
    import numpy as np
    import torch
    from optimum.onnxruntime import ORTModelForSequenceClassification, ORTQuantizer
    from optimum.onnxruntime.configuration import AutoQuantizationConfig
    from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer

    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fp32_dir = out_dir / "fp32"
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(checkpoint)

    print(f"[1/4] exporting {checkpoint} -> ONNX fp32")
    ort_model = ORTModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint, export=True)
    ort_model.save_pretrained(fp32_dir)
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(fp32_dir)

    print("[2/4] dynamic int8 quantization")
    quantizer = ORTQuantizer.from_pretrained(fp32_dir)
    # avx512_vnni=False keeps the graph runnable on any x86 CPU, including the
    # examiner's laptop. The VNNI variant is faster but silently unsupported on
    # older cores, and a demo that will not start is worse than one that is slow.
    qconfig = AutoQuantizationConfig.avx2(is_static=False, per_channel=False)
    quantizer.quantize(save_dir=out_dir, quantization_config=qconfig)
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(out_dir)

    int8_path = next(out_dir.glob("*quantized*.onnx"), None) or next(out_dir.glob("*.onnx"))
    print(f"      int8 graph: {int8_path.name}")

    print(f"[3/4] parity check on {len(pairs)} held-out pairs")
    torch_model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint).eval()
    enc_pt = _tokenize(tokenizer, pairs, max_length, "pt")
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits_torch = torch_model(**enc_pt).logits.numpy()

    enc_np = _tokenize(tokenizer, pairs, max_length, "np")

    import onnxruntime as ort

    def run(path: pathlib.Path) -> Any:
        session = ort.InferenceSession(str(path), providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
        names = {i.name for i in session.get_inputs()}
        feeds = {k: v.astype(np.int64) for k, v in enc_np.items() if k in names}
        return session.run(None, feeds)[0]

    fp32_path = next(fp32_dir.glob("*.onnx"))
    logits_fp32 = run(fp32_path)
    logits_int8 = run(int8_path)

    def compare(name: str, other: Any, tolerance: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
        delta = float(np.abs(logits_torch - other).max())
        agree = int((logits_torch.argmax(-1) == other.argmax(-1)).sum())
        ok = delta <= tolerance and agree == len(pairs)
        print(
            f"      {name:10s} max|dlogit| {delta:.6f} (tol {tolerance})  "
            f"argmax agrees {agree}/{len(pairs)}  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}"
        )
        return {"max_abs_logit_delta": delta, "argmax_agreement": agree,
                "n": len(pairs), "tolerance": tolerance, "pass": ok}

    report = {
        "task": "T-304",
        "checkpoint": checkpoint,
        "labels": list(LABELS),
        "onnx_fp32": compare("ONNX fp32", logits_fp32, FP32_TOLERANCE),
        "onnx_int8": compare("ONNX int8", logits_int8, INT8_TOLERANCE),
        "int8_model": str(int8_path),
        "sizes_mb": {
            "onnx_fp32": round(fp32_path.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2),
            "onnx_int8": round(int8_path.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2),
        },
    }
    print(
        f"[4/4] size: fp32 {report['sizes_mb']['onnx_fp32']} MB "
        f"-> int8 {report['sizes_mb']['onnx_int8']} MB"
    )
    return report


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-304 - ONNX + int8 export with parity check.")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True,
                    help="the unzipped Kaggle output dir, or any HF model id for a dry run")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT)
    ap.add_argument("--pairs", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_PAIRS)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=20, help="held-out pairs for the parity check")
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--keep-fp32", action="store_true",
                    help="keep the intermediate fp32 graph (roughly 4x the int8 size)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    pairs = read_jsonl(args.pairs)[: args.n]
    print(f"T-304 - ONNX export\n  checkpoint: {args.checkpoint}\n  out: {args.out}\n")

    report = export(args.checkpoint, args.out, pairs=pairs, max_length=args.max_length)

    if not args.keep_fp32:
        shutil.rmtree(args.out / "fp32", ignore_errors=True)
        print("      removed the intermediate fp32 graph (--keep-fp32 to retain)")

    report_path = args.out / "export_report.json"
    report_path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {report_path}")

    if not (report["onnx_fp32"]["pass"] and report["onnx_int8"]["pass"]):
        raise SystemExit("T-304 FAILED the parity check - do not ship this export.")
    print("T-304 PASS: the ONNX int8 model reproduces PyTorch decisions on all "
          f"{args.n} held-out pairs.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""T-304 — export the trained verifier to ONNX + int8, and prove it still works.

The pipeline runs on CPU with no torch at inference time (``pyproject.toml``'s
``verify`` extra deliberately omits torch), so the Kaggle checkpoint has to
become an ONNX graph before ``agents/verifier.py`` can use it.

**The acceptance criterion is a parity check, not a successful export.** An
export that silently produces garbage still "succeeds". Two separate checks,
because they fail for different reasons:

``PyTorch -> ONNX fp32``  logits must agree to ~1e-3 **and** argmax 100%.
                          This is the *export correctness* test. Measured
                          2026-08-27 on the stock checkpoint: max |dlogit|
                          **8e-6**, argmax 20/20, and identical macro-F1 on the
                          full 628-pair held-out set (0.516 both ways).

``ONNX fp32 -> int8``     gated on **macro-F1 over the whole held-out set**,
                          not on per-pair argmax.

⚠️ **The int8 gate was originally per-pair argmax agreement on 20 examples, and
that was the wrong test.** Measured on the stock checkpoint, dynamic int8 flips
**2 of 20** individual decisions and moves single logits by up to 4.2 — which
looks alarming — yet over the full 628-pair set it costs *nothing*:

    ONNX fp32               accuracy 0.553   macro-F1 0.516
    int8 per_channel=False  accuracy 0.554   macro-F1 0.538
    int8 per_channel=True   accuracy 0.556   macro-F1 0.539

The flips go both ways and cancel. A 20-sample argmax gate would have rejected
a quantization that is demonstrably free, so the gate now measures the thing
that actually matters. DeBERTa's disentangled attention is genuinely
quantization-sensitive per-logit; it just does not matter in aggregate.

``per_channel=True`` is the default on that evidence — same size, marginally
better, no downside found.

Run::

    # after downloading and unzipping the Kaggle output
    python -m researchgpt.verify.export_onnx --checkpoint data/models/verifier-scifact

    # dry-run the whole path against the stock checkpoint, before Kaggle returns
    python -m researchgpt.verify.export_onnx --checkpoint cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-small
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import shutil
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import encode_pair
from researchgpt.verify.labels import LABELS
from researchgpt.verify.scifact_pairs import read_jsonl

DEFAULT_PAIRS = pathlib.Path("data/scifact/pairs_validation.jsonl")
DEFAULT_OUT = pathlib.Path("data/models/verifier-onnx")

#: ONNX fp32 must be a faithful re-encoding of the PyTorch graph.
FP32_TOLERANCE = 1e-3
#: How far int8 may move macro-F1 on the full held-out set before the export is
#: rejected. Measured drift on the stock checkpoint was +0.022 (an improvement),
#: so 0.03 is roughly "no worse than the noise floor at n=628".
INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE = 0.03


def _tokenize(tokenizer: Any, pairs: list[dict[str, Any]], max_length: int, framework: str):
    return tokenizer(
        [encode_pair(p)[0] for p in pairs],
        [encode_pair(p)[1] for p in pairs],
        padding=True,
        truncation=True,
        max_length=max_length,
        return_tensors=framework,
    )


def export(
    checkpoint: str,
    out_dir: pathlib.Path,
    *,
    pairs: list[dict[str, Any]],
    eval_pairs: list[dict[str, Any]] | None = None,
    max_length: int = 256,
    per_channel: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Export, quantize, and parity-check. Returns the report dict.

    ``pairs`` drives the fast per-logit parity check; ``eval_pairs`` (the full
    held-out set) drives the int8 accuracy gate. Passing ``None`` for the latter
    skips the gate and leaves the export ungated — useful only for a dry run.
    """
    import numpy as np
    import torch
    from optimum.onnxruntime import ORTModelForSequenceClassification, ORTQuantizer
    from optimum.onnxruntime.configuration import AutoQuantizationConfig
    from transformers import AutoModelForSequenceClassification, AutoTokenizer

    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fp32_dir = out_dir / "fp32"
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(checkpoint)

    print(f"[1/4] exporting {checkpoint} -> ONNX fp32")
    ort_model = ORTModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint, export=True)
    ort_model.save_pretrained(fp32_dir)
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(fp32_dir)

    print("[2/4] dynamic int8 quantization")
    quantizer = ORTQuantizer.from_pretrained(fp32_dir)
    # avx512_vnni=False keeps the graph runnable on any x86 CPU, including the
    # examiner's laptop. The VNNI variant is faster but silently unsupported on
    # older cores, and a demo that will not start is worse than one that is slow.
    qconfig = AutoQuantizationConfig.avx2(is_static=False, per_channel=False)
    quantizer.quantize(save_dir=out_dir, quantization_config=qconfig)
    tokenizer.save_pretrained(out_dir)

    int8_path = next(out_dir.glob("*quantized*.onnx"), None) or next(out_dir.glob("*.onnx"))
    print(f"      int8 graph: {int8_path.name}")

    print(f"[3/4] parity check on {len(pairs)} held-out pairs")
    torch_model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(checkpoint).eval()
    enc_pt = _tokenize(tokenizer, pairs, max_length, "pt")
    with torch.no_grad():
        logits_torch = torch_model(**enc_pt).logits.numpy()

    enc_np = _tokenize(tokenizer, pairs, max_length, "np")

    import onnxruntime as ort

    def run(path: pathlib.Path) -> Any:
        session = ort.InferenceSession(str(path), providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
        names = {i.name for i in session.get_inputs()}
        feeds = {k: v.astype(np.int64) for k, v in enc_np.items() if k in names}
        return session.run(None, feeds)[0]

    fp32_path = next(fp32_dir.glob("*.onnx"))
    logits_fp32 = run(fp32_path)
    logits_int8 = run(int8_path)

    def compare(name: str, other: Any, tolerance: float) -> dict[str, Any]:
        delta = float(np.abs(logits_torch - other).max())
        agree = int((logits_torch.argmax(-1) == other.argmax(-1)).sum())
        ok = delta <= tolerance and agree == len(pairs)
        print(
            f"      {name:10s} max|dlogit| {delta:.6f} (tol {tolerance})  "
            f"argmax agrees {agree}/{len(pairs)}  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}"
        )
        return {"max_abs_logit_delta": delta, "argmax_agreement": agree,
                "n": len(pairs), "tolerance": tolerance, "pass": ok}

    report = {
        "task": "T-304",
        "checkpoint": checkpoint,
        "labels": list(LABELS),
        "onnx_fp32": compare("ONNX fp32", logits_fp32, FP32_TOLERANCE),
        "onnx_int8": compare("ONNX int8", logits_int8, INT8_TOLERANCE),
        "int8_model": str(int8_path),
        "sizes_mb": {
            "onnx_fp32": round(fp32_path.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2),
            "onnx_int8": round(int8_path.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2),
        },
    }
    print(
        f"[4/4] size: fp32 {report['sizes_mb']['onnx_fp32']} MB "
        f"-> int8 {report['sizes_mb']['onnx_int8']} MB"
    )
    return report


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-304 - ONNX + int8 export with parity check.")
    ap.add_argument("--checkpoint", required=True,
                    help="the unzipped Kaggle output dir, or any HF model id for a dry run")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT)
    ap.add_argument("--pairs", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_PAIRS)
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=20, help="held-out pairs for the parity check")
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--keep-fp32", action="store_true",
                    help="keep the intermediate fp32 graph (roughly 4x the int8 size)")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    pairs = read_jsonl(args.pairs)[: args.n]
    print(f"T-304 - ONNX export\n  checkpoint: {args.checkpoint}\n  out: {args.out}\n")

    report = export(args.checkpoint, args.out, pairs=pairs, max_length=args.max_length)

    if not args.keep_fp32:
        shutil.rmtree(args.out / "fp32", ignore_errors=True)
        print("      removed the intermediate fp32 graph (--keep-fp32 to retain)")

    report_path = args.out / "export_report.json"
    report_path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {report_path}")

    if not (report["onnx_fp32"]["pass"] and report["onnx_int8"]["pass"]):
        raise SystemExit("T-304 FAILED the parity check - do not ship this export.")
    print("T-304 PASS: the ONNX int8 model reproduces PyTorch decisions on all "
          f"{args.n} held-out pairs.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

        delta = float(np.abs(logits_torch - other).max())

        fp32_parity["max_abs_logit_delta"] <= FP32_TOLERANCE

    )
    print(f"      -> export correctness: {'PASS' if fp32_parity['pass'] else 'FAIL'}")

    # int8 per-logit drift is recorded but NOT gated on: it is large per-pair and
    # ~zero in aggregate. See the module docstring for the measurement.
    int8_parity = logit_delta("ONNX int8", logits_int8)

    report: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task": "T-304",
        "checkpoint": checkpoint,
        "labels": list(LABELS),
        "per_channel": per_channel,
        "onnx_fp32": fp32_parity,
        "onnx_int8_logit_drift": int8_parity,
        "int8_model": str(int8_path),
        "sizes_mb": {
            "onnx_fp32": round(fp32_path.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2),
            "onnx_int8": round(int8_path.stat().st_size / 1e6, 2),
        },
    }
    print(
        f"[4/4] size: fp32 {report['sizes_mb']['onnx_fp32']} MB "
        f"-> int8 {report['sizes_mb']['onnx_int8']} MB"
    )

    if eval_pairs:
        from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import predict_onnx, score
        from researchgpt.verify.labels import LABEL2ID

        print(f"\n[gate] int8 accuracy over the full held-out set ({len(eval_pairs)} pairs)")
        y_true = [LABEL2ID[p["label"]] for p in eval_pairs]
        fp32_score = score(y_true, predict_onnx(str(fp32_path), str(fp32_dir), eval_pairs))
        int8_score = score(y_true, predict_onnx(str(int8_path), str(out_dir), eval_pairs))
        drop = fp32_score["macro_f1"] - int8_score["macro_f1"]
        passed = drop <= INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE
        print(f"      fp32  accuracy {fp32_score['accuracy']:.3f}  "
              f"macro-F1 {fp32_score['macro_f1']:.3f}")
        print(f"      int8  accuracy {int8_score['accuracy']:.3f}  "
              f"macro-F1 {int8_score['macro_f1']:.3f}")
        print(f"      macro-F1 lost to quantization: {drop:+.3f} "
              f"(tolerance {INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE})  {'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}")
        report["int8_accuracy_gate"] = {
            "fp32": {"accuracy": fp32_score["accuracy"], "macro_f1": fp32_score["macro_f1"]},
            "int8": {"accuracy": int8_score["accuracy"], "macro_f1": int8_score["macro_f1"]},
            "macro_f1_drop": drop,
            "tolerance": INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE,
            "n": len(eval_pairs),
            "pass": passed,
        }

    return report

"""T-306 — per-claim CPU latency for the int8 verifier.

TASKLIST's framing: a full run makes roughly 1,500–2,000 verifier forward
passes, so the number that matters is **claims/sec on this machine**, not
milliseconds in isolation. At 20/sec the verification stage is ~100 s; at 2/sec
it is ~15 minutes and starts to compete with the ~30-minute budget in §0.2.

Measures three things, because they answer different questions:

* **batch=1 latency** — what a single interactive verification costs, which is
  what the Vue evidence panel (T-607) would pay on a click.
* **batched throughput** — what the pipeline actually gets, since T-504 verifies
  a whole draft's claims at once and can batch freely.
* **tokenization share** — DeBERTa's SentencePiece tokenizer is not free, and if
  it dominates then batching the *model* is the wrong optimisation.

Run::

    python -m researchgpt.verify.benchmark --model data/models/verifier-onnx
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import encode_pair
from researchgpt.verify.scifact_pairs import read_jsonl

DEFAULT_PAIRS = pathlib.Path("data/scifact/pairs_validation.jsonl")


def _find_onnx(model_dir: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    candidate = next(model_dir.glob("*quantized*.onnx"), None) or next(
        model_dir.glob("*.onnx"), None
    )
    if candidate is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"no .onnx file under {model_dir}")
    return candidate


def benchmark(
    model_dir: pathlib.Path,
    pairs: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    batch_sizes: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 8, 16, 32),
    max_length: int = 256,
    warmup: int = 3,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    import numpy as np
    import onnxruntime as ort
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    onnx_path = _find_onnx(model_dir)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(model_dir))

    # Default session options: one intra-op thread pool sized by ORT. The
    # pipeline shares the CPU with embedding and reranking, so pinning threads
    # here would just move the contention somewhere less visible.
    session = ort.InferenceSession(str(onnx_path), providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
    input_names = {i.name for i in session.get_inputs()}

    print(f"model : {onnx_path.name}  ({onnx_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    print(f"pairs : {len(pairs)}  max_length={max_length}")
    print(f"onnxruntime {ort.__version__}, providers={session.get_providers()}\n")

    def tokenize(batch: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        enc = tokenizer(
            [encode_pair(p)[0] for p in batch],
            [encode_pair(p)[1] for p in batch],
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            return_tensors="np",
        )
        return {k: v.astype(np.int64) for k, v in enc.items() if k in input_names}

    # Warm up: the first few calls pay graph-init and allocator costs that would
    # otherwise be charged to the batch=1 arm and make it look 3x worse.
    for _ in range(warmup):
        session.run(None, tokenize(pairs[:8]))

    results: dict[str, Any] = {}
    print(f"  {'batch':>6s} {'claims/sec':>11s} {'ms/claim':>10s} {'ms/batch p50':>13s}")
    for batch_size in batch_sizes:
        batches = [pairs[i : i + batch_size] for i in range(0, len(pairs), batch_size)]
        # batch=1 over the whole set is slow and adds nothing after ~200 samples.
        if batch_size == 1:
            batches = batches[:200]

        times: list[float] = []
        tokenize_time = 0.0
        start_all = time.perf_counter()
        n_claims = 0
        for batch in batches:
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            feeds = tokenize(batch)
            t1 = time.perf_counter()
            session.run(None, feeds)
            t2 = time.perf_counter()
            tokenize_time += t1 - t0
            times.append(t2 - t0)
            n_claims += len(batch)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start_all

        per_sec = n_claims / elapsed
        results[str(batch_size)] = {
            "claims_per_sec": per_sec,
            "ms_per_claim": 1000 * elapsed / n_claims,
            "ms_per_batch_p50": 1000 * statistics.median(times),
            "tokenize_share": tokenize_time / elapsed,
            "n_claims": n_claims,
        }
        print(
            f"  {batch_size:6d} {per_sec:11.1f} {1000 * elapsed / n_claims:10.2f} "
            f"{1000 * statistics.median(times):13.2f}"
        )

    best = max(results.values(), key=lambda r: r["claims_per_sec"])
    print(f"\n  tokenization is {best['tokenize_share']:.0%} of wall time at the best batch size")
    return results


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-306 - CPU throughput of the int8 verifier.")
    ap.add_argument("--model", type=pathlib.Path, required=True,
                    help="directory holding the quantized .onnx and its tokenizer")
    ap.add_argument("--pairs", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_PAIRS)
    ap.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--max-length", type=int, default=256)
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path, default=pathlib.Path("eval/verifier_latency_t306.json"))
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    pairs = read_jsonl(args.pairs)[: args.limit]
    print("T-306 - verifier CPU throughput\n")
    results = benchmark(args.model, pairs, max_length=args.max_length)

    best_bs, best = max(results.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]["claims_per_sec"])
    rate = best["claims_per_sec"]
    # TASKLIST's own sizing: a full run is ~1.5-2k forward passes.
    print("\n" + "=" * 66)
    print(f"BEST: {rate:.1f} claims/sec at batch={best_bs}")
    for passes in (1500, 2000):
        print(f"  a {passes}-claim run spends {passes / rate:6.1f} s "
              f"({passes / rate / 60:.1f} min) in the verifier")
    print("=" * 66)
    if rate < 20:
        print("NOTE: below TASKLIST T-306's 20/sec reference point. Verification becomes a "
              "visible share of the ~30 min budget (0.2); consider batching harder in T-502.")
    else:
        print("Comfortably above T-306's 20/sec reference point.")

    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(
        json.dumps({"task": "T-306", "model": str(args.model), "results": results}, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    print(f"\nwrote {args.out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""T-306 — per-claim CPU latency for the int8 verifier.

TASKLIST's framing: a full run makes roughly 1,500–2,000 verifier forward
passes, so the number that matters is **claims/sec on this machine**, not
milliseconds in isolation. At 20/sec the verification stage is ~100 s; at 2/sec
it is ~15 minutes and starts to compete with the ~30-minute budget in §0.2.

Measures three things, because they answer different questions:

* **batch=1 latency** — what a single interactive verification costs, which is
  what the Vue evidence panel (T-607) would pay on a click.
* **batched throughput** — what the pipeline actually gets, since T-504 verifies
  a whole draft's claims at once and can batch freely.
* **tokenization share** — DeBERTa's SentencePiece tokenizer is not free, and if
  it dominates then batching the *model* is the wrong optimisation.

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import encode_pair
from researchgpt.verify.scifact_pairs import read_jsonl

DEFAULT_PAIRS = pathlib.Path("data/scifact/pairs_validation.jsonl")


def _find_onnx(model_dir: pathlib.Path) -> pathlib.Path:
    candidate = next(model_dir.glob("*quantized*.onnx"), None) or next(
        model_dir.glob("*.onnx"), None
    )
    if candidate is None:
        raise SystemExit(f"no .onnx file under {model_dir}")
    return candidate


def benchmark(
    model_dir: pathlib.Path,
    pairs: list[dict[str, Any]],
    *,
    batch_sizes: tuple[int, ...] = (1, 8, 16, 32),
    max_length: int = 256,
    warmup: int = 3,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    import numpy as np
    import onnxruntime as ort
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer

    onnx_path = _find_onnx(model_dir)
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(str(model_dir))

    # Default session options: one intra-op thread pool sized by ORT. The
    # pipeline shares the CPU with embedding and reranking, so pinning threads
    # here would just move the contention somewhere less visible.
    session = ort.InferenceSession(str(onnx_path), providers=["CPUExecutionProvider"])
    input_names = {i.name for i in session.get_inputs()}

    print(f"model : {onnx_path.name}  ({onnx_path.stat().st_size / 1e6:.1f} MB)")
    print(f"pairs : {len(pairs)}  max_length={max_length}")

            [encode_pair(p)[0] for p in batch],
            [encode_pair(p)[1] for p in batch],
            padding=True,
            truncation=True,
            max_length=max_length,
            return_tensors="np",
        )

    # Warm up: the first few calls pay graph-init and allocator costs that would
    # otherwise be charged to the batch=1 arm and make it look 3x worse.
    for _ in range(warmup):
        session.run(None, tokenize(pairs[:8]))

    results: dict[str, Any] = {}
    print(f"  {'batch':>6s} {'claims/sec':>11s} {'ms/claim':>10s} {'ms/batch p50':>13s}")

            "ms_per_batch_p50": 1000 * statistics.median(times),
            "tokenize_share": tokenize_time / elapsed,
            "n_claims": n_claims,

        print(
            f"  {batch_size:6d} {per_sec:11.1f} {1000 * elapsed / n_claims:10.2f} "
            f"{1000 * statistics.median(times):13.2f}"
        )

    best = max(results.values(), key=lambda r: r["claims_per_sec"])
    print(f"\n  tokenization is {best['tokenize_share']:.0%} of wall time at the best batch size")
    return results

    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-306 - CPU throughput of the int8 verifier.")
    ap.add_argument("--model", type=pathlib.Path, required=True,

    for passes in (1500, 2000):
        print(f"  a {passes}-claim run spends {passes / rate:6.1f} s "

    print("=" * 66)
    if rate < 20:
        print("NOTE: below TASKLIST T-306's 20/sec reference point. Verification becomes a "

"""Phase 3 acceptance tests — the verifier training track (T-301..T-307).

Everything here runs offline against synthetic rows except the tests marked
``network``, so the suite stays fast and works on a plane. The synthetic rows
mirror the real SciFact shape verified on 2026-08-27:

    claim_id repeats across rows, `abstract` is a sentence list, `evidence`
    holds indices into it and is empty exactly when verdict == "NEI".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib

import pytest

from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import (
    ESCALATION_THRESHOLD,
    encode_pair,
    escalation_verdict,
    label_permutation,
    score,
)
from researchgpt.verify.labels import ID2LABEL, LABEL2ID, LABELS
from researchgpt.verify.scifact_pairs import build_pairs, class_counts, split_by_claim

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
NOTEBOOK = REPO / "notebook-kaggle-traning" / "01_train_verifier_scifact.ipynb"


def _row(claim_id, verdict, evidence, n_sents=6, abstract_id=None):
    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "claim": f"claim number {claim_id}",
        "abstract_id": abstract_id if abstract_id is not None else claim_id * 10,
        "title": "t",
        "abstract": [f"sentence {i}" for i in range(n_sents)],
        "verdict": verdict,
        "evidence": evidence,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# T-301 — pairing
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_t301_support_emits_one_pair_per_evidence_sentence():
    pairs = build_pairs([_row(1, "SUPPORT", [0, 3, 5])])
    assert len(pairs) == 3
    assert [p["sentence_index"] for p in pairs] == [0, 3, 5]
    assert {p["evidence"] for p in pairs} == {"sentence 0", "sentence 3", "sentence 5"}
    assert all(p["label"] == "SUPPORT" for p in pairs)


def test_t301_nei_samples_from_the_abstract():
    """NEI rows carry no evidence, so sentences are sampled — `nei_per_claim` of them."""
    pairs = build_pairs([_row(1, "NEI", [])], nei_per_claim=2)
    assert len(pairs) == 2
    assert all(p["label"] == "NEI" for p in pairs)
    assert all(p["evidence"].startswith("sentence ") for p in pairs)
    assert len({p["sentence_index"] for p in pairs}) == 2, "sampled without replacement"


def test_t301_nei_sampling_is_capped_by_abstract_length():
    pairs = build_pairs([_row(1, "NEI", [], n_sents=1)], nei_per_claim=5)
    assert len(pairs) == 1


def test_t301_is_deterministic_under_a_fixed_seed():
    rows = [_row(i, "NEI", []) for i in range(20)]
    assert build_pairs(rows, seed=7) == build_pairs(rows, seed=7)
    assert build_pairs(rows, seed=7) != build_pairs(rows, seed=8)


def test_t301_out_of_range_evidence_index_is_dropped_not_crashed():
    """Defensive: an index past the end of `abstract` must not raise or emit junk."""
    pairs = build_pairs([_row(1, "SUPPORT", [0, 99])])
    assert len(pairs) == 1
    assert pairs[0]["sentence_index"] == 0


def test_t301_non_nei_row_with_no_usable_evidence_emits_nothing():
    """Better to drop the row than to emit a pair whose label is unsupported by
    any sentence — that would be a silently mislabelled training example."""
    assert build_pairs([_row(1, "SUPPORT", [])]) == []
    assert build_pairs([_row(1, "SUPPORT", [42])]) == []


def test_t301_split_never_leaks_a_claim_across_the_boundary():
    """The regression that matters. One claim spans several rows, so a row-level
    split puts the same claim text on both sides and inflates the dev score."""
    rows = []
    for claim_id in range(40):
        for abstract in range(3):  # same claim, three different abstracts
            rows.append(_row(claim_id, "SUPPORT", [0, 1], abstract_id=claim_id * 10 + abstract))
    pairs = build_pairs(rows)
    train, dev = split_by_claim(pairs, dev_frac=0.25)

    assert train and dev
    assert not ({p["claim_id"] for p in train} & {p["claim_id"] for p in dev})
    assert len(train) + len(dev) == len(pairs)


def test_t301_split_keeps_every_pair_of_a_held_out_claim_together():
    rows = [_row(1, "SUPPORT", [0, 1, 2]), _row(1, "SUPPORT", [3], abstract_id=99)]
    pairs = build_pairs(rows)
    train, dev = split_by_claim(pairs, dev_frac=1.0)
    assert len(dev) == len(pairs) and not train


def test_t301_class_counts_cover_every_label():
    counts = class_counts(build_pairs([_row(1, "SUPPORT", [0])]))
    assert set(counts) == set(LABELS)
    assert counts["CONTRADICT"] == 0, "absent classes report 0, not a missing key"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Label vocabulary and the head permutation
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_labels_round_trip():
    assert LABELS == ("SUPPORT", "CONTRADICT", "NEI")
    for i, label in enumerate(LABELS):
        assert LABEL2ID[label] == i and ID2LABEL[i] == label


def test_permutation_maps_the_stock_nli_head_onto_our_order():
    """The stock checkpoint is {0: contradiction, 1: entailment, 2: neutral}.
    Verified live against `cross-encoder/nli-deberta-v3-small` on 2026-08-27."""
    stock = {0: "contradiction", 1: "entailment", 2: "neutral"}
    assert label_permutation(stock) == [1, 0, 2]


def test_permutation_is_identity_for_a_checkpoint_already_in_our_vocabulary():
    assert label_permutation({0: "SUPPORT", 1: "CONTRADICT", 2: "NEI"}) == [0, 1, 2]


def test_permutation_refuses_to_guess_on_an_unknown_head():
    """A wrong permutation is invisible in the output and poisons every number
    downstream, so an unrecognised head must raise rather than default."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Cannot map checkpoint label"):
        label_permutation({0: "LABEL_0", 1: "LABEL_1", 2: "LABEL_2"})


def test_permutation_rejects_an_incomplete_head():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="missing"):
        label_permutation({0: "entailment", 1: "neutral"})


def test_encode_pair_puts_evidence_first():
    """Premise = evidence, hypothesis = claim. Reversing them silently trains a
    different task, so the order is pinned by a test rather than a comment."""
    premise, hypothesis = encode_pair({"claim": "C", "evidence": "E"})
    assert (premise, hypothesis) == ("E", "C")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# T-305 scoring
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_score_is_perfect_on_perfect_predictions():
    y = [0, 1, 2, 0, 1, 2]
    result = score(y, y)
    assert result["accuracy"] == 1.0
    assert result["macro_f1"] == 1.0
    assert all(m["f1"] == 1.0 for m in result["per_class"].values())


def test_score_reports_zero_not_nan_for_a_class_never_predicted():
    """A model that never predicts CONTRADICT must score 0 there, not NaN —
    NaN would silently poison the macro average the T-307 gate reads."""
    y_true = [0, 1, 2]
    y_pred = [0, 0, 2]
    result = score(y_true, y_pred)
    assert result["per_class"]["CONTRADICT"]["f1"] == 0.0
    assert result["macro_f1"] == result["macro_f1"]  # not NaN


def test_score_confusion_matrix_orientation():
    """Rows are true, columns predicted. Getting this backwards inverts every
    precision/recall pair, which reads as plausible but is wrong."""
    result = score([0, 0], [2, 2])
    assert result["confusion"][0][2] == 2
    assert result["confusion"][2][0] == 0
    assert result["per_class"]["SUPPORT"]["recall"] == 0.0


def test_score_support_counts_are_true_class_totals():
    result = score([0, 0, 0, 1], [0, 1, 2, 1])
    assert result["per_class"]["SUPPORT"]["support"] == 3
    assert result["per_class"]["CONTRADICT"]["support"] == 1


def test_score_rejects_mismatched_lengths():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        score([0, 1], [0])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# T-307 escalation gate
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_t307_gate_threshold_matches_the_recorded_decision():
    """decisions.txt D-09 fixed this at 0.75 BEFORE the first training run.
    If someone edits the constant after seeing a result, this fails."""
    assert ESCALATION_THRESHOLD == 0.75

    return {
        "claim_id": claim_id,
        "claim": f"claim number {claim_id}",
        "abstract_id": abstract_id if abstract_id is not None else claim_id * 10,
        "title": "t",

    assert {p["evidence"] for p in pairs} == {"sentence 0", "sentence 3", "sentence 5"}
    assert all(p["label"] == "SUPPORT" for p in pairs)

    pairs = build_pairs([_row(1, "NEI", [])], nei_per_claim=2)
    assert len(pairs) == 2
    assert all(p["label"] == "NEI" for p in pairs)
    assert all(p["evidence"].startswith("sentence ") for p in pairs)
    assert len({p["sentence_index"] for p in pairs}) == 2, "sampled without replacement"

# Kaggle training notebooks

Every GPU training run in ResearchGPT lives here. Each notebook is
self-contained: it downloads its own data, trains, evaluates, applies its
adoption/escalation gate and writes a metrics JSON. Nothing in this folder
needs the `researchgpt` package to be installed on Kaggle.

| Notebook | Task | Trains | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `01_train_verifier_scifact.ipynb` | **T-302 / T-303** | The claim verifier (`deberta-v3-small`, 3-way NLI) | **Ready to run** |
| `02_train_reranker_scireviewgen.ipynb` | T-332 | The cross-encoder reranker | Blocked — needs Phase 3B (T-330/T-331 build its triples) |

> **Why the verifier goes first.** It is the graded component *and* the
> required training component. TASKLIST T-332 says so explicitly: *"Train the
> verifier (T-303) first — it is the graded component and takes priority on the
> quota."* The reranker is a weight swap that the pipeline never depends on.

---

## 01 — Verifier fine-tune (T-302 / T-303)

Trains the three-way claim verifier that decides `SUPPORT` / `CONTRADICT` /
`NEI` for a drafted claim against a retrieved evidence sentence.

### Before you start

Nothing. The notebook builds its own data from the Hugging Face Hub. You do
**not** need to upload the local `data/scifact/*.jsonl` — those are built by the

32	**Pairing rule** (TASKLIST T-301):

35	  ``evidence``. A 3-sentence evidence set becomes 3 training pairs.

37	  that row's abstract. The abstract is a genuine retrieved-but-non-supporting
38	  abstract for that claim, so its sentences really are "not enough info".

105	        repo_type="dataset",
106	        revision=_REVISION,
107	    )

132	    Rows are processed in file order and the RNG is seeded once, so the output

154	                # emitting a mislabelled pair is the worse failure.
155	                continue
156	
157	        for i in indices:
158	            pairs.append(
159	                {

162	                    "label": verdict,
163	                    "claim_id": row["claim_id"],
164	                    "abstract_id": row["abstract_id"],

67	    """Column indices that reorder a checkpoint's logits into ``LABELS`` order.
68

72	    or a stock NLI head (``entailment``/``contradiction``/``neutral``). Raises
73	    on anything else rather than guessing — a wrong permutation is invisible in
74	    the output and poisons every number downstream.
75	    """
76	    normalised: dict[str, int] = {}
77	    for idx, raw in id2label.items():
78	        name = str(raw).strip()
79	        verdict = name.upper() if name.upper() in LABEL2ID else NLI_TO_VERDICT.get(name.lower())
80	        if verdict is None:

82	                f"Cannot map checkpoint label {raw!r} onto {LABELS}. "
83	                f"Checkpoint id2label={id2label}. Refusing to guess a permutation."
84	            )
85	        normalised[verdict] = int(idx)
86	
87	    missing = [label for label in LABELS if label not in normalised]
88	    if missing:

114	    model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_path)

2	
3	TASKLIST's framing: a full run makes roughly 1,500–2,000 verifier forward

6	it is ~15 minutes and starts to compete with the ~30-minute budget in §0.2.
7

9	
10	* **batch=1 latency** — what a single interactive verification costs, which is
11	  what the Vue evidence panel (T-607) would pay on a click.
12	* **batched throughput** — what the pipeline actually gets, since T-504 verifies
13	  a whole draft's claims at once and can batch freely.
14	* **tokenization share** — DeBERTa's SentencePiece tokenizer is not free, and if
15	  it dominates then batching the *model* is the wrong optimisation.

143	        )
144	
145	    best = max(results.values(), key=lambda r: r["claims_per_sec"])
146	    print(f"\n  tokenization is {best['tokenize_share']:.0%} of wall time at the best batch size")
147	    return results

Phase 3 is complete except the one step only you can run.

## What's done

| Task | Status |
|---|---|
| **T-301** pairs | ✅ 1463 train / 272 dev / **628 held-out** |
| **T-302** notebook | ✅ `01_train_verifier_scifact.ipynb`, all 11 cells smoke-tested locally |
| **T-303** Kaggle run | ⏳ **yours** — ready to upload |
| **T-304** ONNX int8 | ✅ verified end-to-end, 568 MB → 172 MB |
| **T-305** stock-vs-tuned | ✅ harness + **stock row already measured** |
| **T-306** CPU latency | ✅ **33.3 claims/sec** |
| **T-307** escalation gate | ✅ threshold fixed at 0.75 *before* any run |

**53 tests pass**, lint clean, and I confirmed the Phase 2 suite still passes after the dependency install.

## Your one step

Upload `notebook-kaggle-traning/01_train_verifier_scifact.ipynb`, set **Accelerator = GPU T4 x2** and **Internet = On** in the Settings panel, Run All. ~10–20 min. Full walkthrough in `notebook-kaggle-traning/README.md`.

Kaggle silently ignores a notebook's requested accelerator on import — set it yourself and confirm it says GPU, or you'll wait an hour to find it ran on CPU.

**Sanity check while it runs:** section 7 must print **accuracy 0.553, macro-F1 0.516**. I measured that locally, so if Kaggle prints something materially different, the data or the label permutation moved — stop rather than trust the trained number.

## Four things worth your attention

**TASKLIST's T-301 instruction was wrong and would have blocked the task.** It says use `scifact_entailment` *because* plain `scifact` is script-based. `scifact_entailment` is script-based too — `datasets>=4` refuses it outright. The 2026-08-25 pre-check passed because it probed the datasets-server API, not `load_dataset`. Fixed by reading the Hub's auto-converted parquet branch.

**The warm start you flagged as "easy to get wrong" — here's the trap.** The stock head is `{0: contradiction, 1: entailment, 2: neutral}`, not our order. The notebook **permutes** it `[1,0,2]` instead of reinitialising, so training starts from a model that already solves two-thirds of the problem. The same permutation is what makes T-305's stock arm a fair baseline rather than a near-chance strawman.

**T-304's stated acceptance criterion is the wrong test.** "Reproduces PyTorch logits on 20 examples" — int8 flips 2 of 20 decisions and moves single logits by up to 4.0. Taken literally, that's a FAIL. But over the full 628-pair set int8 costs *nothing*: macro-F1 0.516 → 0.539. The flips cancel. I re-gated on full-set accuracy and kept the 20-pair check only as an export-correctness test, where a tight tolerance genuinely belongs.

**A design instruction for T-502, from the latency numbers: don't batch the verifier.** Batch=1 gives 33.3 claims/sec; batch=32 gives 10.0 — 3.3× slower. Padding waste plus ORT's already-threaded int8 kernels. The "always batch" instinct from GPU training is actively wrong here.

Also: the stock model's failure mode is more interesting than its F1. SUPPORT recall is **0.234** — it predicts NEI for 158 of 235 true SUPPORT pairs while holding SUPPORT precision at 0.887. Untuned, the verifier is a filter that discards most true claims: safe, and useless. That's a better story for the report than a bare F1 delta, and it's the concrete thing the fine-tune has to fix.

Two caveats. The notebook carries a **copy** of the pairing code since Kaggle can't import your repo — I added a test that execs the notebook's own cells and asserts byte-identical output, and verified it goes red when I sabotage the notebook's seed or sampling rule. And installing the `verify` extra pins `transformers` down to 4.57.6, which pip reports as conflicting with `sentence-transformers` — I checked, it's harmless, all 26 Phase 2 tests still pass. Don't "fix" it by upgrading; that breaks the ONNX path instead.

You chose **D-01 = A (full scope)**, so Phase 3C's reranker notebook is also owed — but T-330/T-331 build its training triples from the Phase 3B parser, which doesn't exist yet. That notebook has to wait for 3B. Nothing is committed; say the word and I'll commit.

import statistics

from transformers import AutoTokenizer

content.text:
While that finishes — the finding reframed, because it changes what the right fix is.

**The model passes; the deployment doesn't.**

- PyTorch / ONNX fp32: macro-F1 **0.769** → passes the 0.75 gate
- ONNX int8 (what would actually ship): macro-F1 **0.741** → **fails it**

T-307's escalation path is "retrain at `deberta-v3-base`." That would be solving the wrong problem. Model *capacity* is fine — 0.769 clears the bar with room. The 0.027 is lost entirely in quantization, and a bigger model quantized the same way would likely lose a similar slice. Escalating buys a 4× training cost to fix something that isn't broken.

The cheaper fix is to not quantize, or to quantize better. TASKLIST §0.2 states the tie-break directly — *"trade latency, not accuracy — the verifier is the graded component"* — and verification is only ~60 s of a ~30 min run, so there's latency to spend. I'm measuring whether fp32 is affordable rather than assuming it.

Note also that neither `decisions.txt` D-09 nor T-307 says *which artefact* the gate applies to. That ambiguity is what let a passing model produce a failing deployment, and it's worth pinning down in the TASKLIST regardless of which way you go.

import pathlib

p = pathlib.Path("src/researchgpt/verify/export_onnx.py")
s = p.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
orig = s

# ---- docstring: record the measurement that flipped the default ----
old = """``per_channel=True`` is the default on that evidence -- same size, marginally
better, no downside found."""
old = old.replace("--", "—")
assert old in s, "docstring anchor"
new = """⚠️ **Measured again on the FINE-TUNED checkpoint (2026-08-27), the conclusion
reversed — and the shipped artefact is now fp32, not int8.** The stock model
happened to be quantization-tolerant; the trained one is not:

    arm                     macro-F1   vs 0.75 gate   claims/sec   size
    fp32                       0.769   PASS                 41.9   568 MB
    int8 per_channel=True      0.741   FAIL                 52.3   173 MB
    int8 per_channel=False     0.741   FAIL                 20.5   173 MB

**int8 drops the deployed model below the T-307 gate that the trained model
passes.** All int8 buys is 10 seconds per run (48 s vs 38 s for 2,000 claims,
against a ~30-minute budget) and 400 MB of disk. `TASKLIST` §0.2 and
`PROJECT_PLAN` §4.2 both say the same thing about exactly this trade — *"trade
latency, not accuracy — the verifier is the graded component"* — so fp32 wins on
the project's own stated rule, not on preference.

This export therefore keeps **both** graphs, gates each on macro-F1, and records
``recommended_model`` in the report. Pass ``--ship int8`` to override.

*(`per_channel=False` is strictly dominated: same accuracy, half the speed.)*"""
s = s.replace(old, new)

# ---- gate section: evaluate both, recommend one ----
old = """        drop = fp32_score["macro_f1"] - int8_score["macro_f1"]
        passed = drop <= INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE
        print(f"      fp32  accuracy {fp32_score['accuracy']:.3f}  "
              f"macro-F1 {fp32_score['macro_f1']:.3f}")
        print(f"      int8  accuracy {int8_score['accuracy']:.3f}  "
              f"macro-F1 {int8_score['macro_f1']:.3f}")
        print(f"      macro-F1 lost to quantization: {drop:+.3f} "
              f"(tolerance {INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE})  {'PASS' if passed else 'FAIL'}")
        report["int8_accuracy_gate"] = {
            "fp32": {"accuracy": fp32_score["accuracy"], "macro_f1": fp32_score["macro_f1"]},
            "int8": {"accuracy": int8_score["accuracy"], "macro_f1": int8_score["macro_f1"]},
            "macro_f1_drop": drop,
            "tolerance": INT8_MACRO_F1_TOLERANCE,
            "n": len(eval_pairs),
            "pass": passed,
        }"""
assert old in s, "gate anchor"
new = """        drop = fp32_score["macro_f1"] - int8_score["macro_f1"]
        # ⚠️ Gate each artefact against T-307 directly. Gating only on the *drop*
        # was the earlier mistake: a small drop still lands the shipped model
        # under the gate when the trained model sits close to it.
        fp32_ok = fp32_score["macro_f1"] >= ESCALATION_THRESHOLD
        int8_ok = int8_score["macro_f1"] >= ESCALATION_THRESHOLD
        for name, sc, ok in (("fp32", fp32_score, fp32_ok), ("int8", int8_score, int8_ok)):
            print(f"      {name}  accuracy {sc['accuracy']:.3f}  "
                  f"macro-F1 {sc['macro_f1']:.3f}  "
                  f"vs T-307 gate {ESCALATION_THRESHOLD}: {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
        print(f"      macro-F1 lost to quantization: {drop:+.3f}")

        if int8_ok:
            recommended = "int8"
            why = "int8 clears the T-307 gate and is smaller and faster"
        elif fp32_ok:
            recommended = "fp32"
            why = (f"int8 falls to {int8_score['macro_f1']:.3f}, under the "
                   f"{ESCALATION_THRESHOLD} gate that fp32 clears. TASKLIST 0.2: "
                   f"trade latency, not accuracy - the verifier is the graded component")
        else:
            recommended = "fp32"
            why = "NEITHER artefact clears the T-307 gate - escalate the model (T-307)"

        report["int8_accuracy_gate"] = {
            "fp32": {"accuracy": fp32_score["accuracy"], "macro_f1": fp32_score["macro_f1"],
                     "pass": fp32_ok},
            "int8": {"accuracy": int8_score["accuracy"], "macro_f1": int8_score["macro_f1"],
                     "pass": int8_ok},
            "macro_f1_drop": drop,
            "t307_threshold": ESCALATION_THRESHOLD,
            "n": len(eval_pairs),
            "pass": fp32_ok or int8_ok,
        }
        report["recommended_model"] = recommended
        report["recommended_reason"] = why
        report["recommended_path"] = str(fp32_path if recommended == "fp32" else int8_path)
        print(f"\\n      SHIP: {recommended}  ({why})")"""
s = s.replace(old, new)

# ---- import the threshold ----
old = "from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import encode_pair"
assert old in s
s = s.replace(old, "from researchgpt.verify.evaluate import ESCALATION_THRESHOLD, encode_pair")

# ---- CLI: keep fp32 by default ----
old = """    ap.add_argument("--keep-fp32", action="store_true",
                    help="keep the intermediate fp32 graph (roughly 3x the int8 size)")"""
assert old in s, "cli anchor"
new = """    ap.add_argument("--discard-fp32", action="store_true",
                    help="delete the fp32 graph after exporting. ONLY safe if int8 clears "
                         "the T-307 gate - on the 2026-08-27 checkpoint it does not.")"""
s = s.replace(old, new)

old = """    if not args.keep_fp32:
        shutil.rmtree(args.out / "fp32", ignore_errors=True)
        print("\\n      removed the intermediate fp32 graph (--keep-fp32 to retain)")"""
assert old in s, "rmtree anchor"
new = """    if args.discard_fp32:
        shutil.rmtree(args.out / "fp32", ignore_errors=True)
        print("\\n      removed the fp32 graph as requested")"""
s = s.replace(old, new)

# ---- final verdict text ----
old = """    gate = report.get("int8_accuracy_gate")
    if gate and not gate["pass"]:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"T-304 FAILED: int8 costs {gate['macro_f1_drop']:.3f} macro-F1, over the "
            f"{gate['tolerance']} tolerance. Re-export with --no-per-channel, or ship fp32."
        )
    if gate:
        print(f"\\nT-304 PASS: export is faithful and int8 costs "
              f"{gate['macro_f1_drop']:+.3f} macro-F1 over {gate['n']} held-out pairs.")
    else:
        print("\\nT-304 PARTIAL: export is faithful, but --quick skipped the int8 "
              "accuracy gate. Re-run without --quick before shipping.")"""
assert old in s, "verdict anchor"
new = """    gate = report.get("int8_accuracy_gate")
    if gate and not gate["pass"]:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"T-304 FAILED: neither fp32 ({gate['fp32']['macro_f1']:.3f}) nor int8 "
            f"({gate['int8']['macro_f1']:.3f}) clears the T-307 gate of "
            f"{gate['t307_threshold']}. This is a MODEL problem, not an export problem - "
            f"escalate to deberta-v3-base per T-307."
        )
    if gate:
        rec = report["recommended_model"]
        print(f"\\nT-304 PASS: export is faithful. SHIP THE {rec.upper()} MODEL:")
        print(f"  {report['recommended_path']}")
        print(f"  reason: {report['recommended_reason']}")
    else:
        print("\\nT-304 PARTIAL: export is faithful, but --quick skipped the accuracy "
              "gate. Re-run without --quick before shipping.")"""
s = s.replace(old, new)

assert s != orig
p.write_text(s, encoding="utf-8")
print("export_onnx.py: fp32 is now the shipped default, both artefacts gated on T-307")

**Phase 3 is complete** — all seven tasks ticked. 53 tests pass, lint clean.

## The result

| arm | accuracy | macro-F1 | SUPPORT F1 | CONTRADICT F1 | NEI F1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stock | 0.553 | 0.516 | 0.370 | 0.542 | 0.634 |
| **fine-tuned** | **0.788** | **0.769** | **0.783** | **0.672** | **0.851** |
| delta | +0.236 | **+0.253** | +0.412 | +0.130 | +0.217 |

Kaggle (GPU) and my local recomputation (CPU) agree to **six decimals** on both arms, so this table is independently reproduced rather than copied from notebook output.

**Lead the report with the failure mode, not the delta.** Stock SUPPORT recall was 0.234 — it predicted NEI for 158 of 235 true SUPPORT pairs. Tuned, that's 0.766. The stock model isn't merely weaker; it's unusable in the role, because a claim filter that discards two-thirds of true claims leaves you with an empty survey. That argument carries more weight than "+0.25 macro-F1."

## Two findings that changed decisions

**int8 quantization would have shipped a model that fails your own gate.** fp32 scores 0.769; int8 scores **0.741** — below the 0.75 threshold. On the *stock* checkpoint int8 had been free (it actually gained 0.024), so this reversed once the model was fine-tuned. I've made **fp32 the shipped artefact**. It costs 400 MB and ~35 s per run (79 s vs 44 s, against a ~30-minute budget) and follows your own written rule — §0.2 and PROJECT_PLAN §4.2 both say *"trade latency, not accuracy — the verifier is the graded component."*

Note this is a deviation from T-304 as written ("export to ONNX + int8"). It's reversible: `export_report.json` names the recommended model, and T-502 should read that path rather than hard-code a filename.

Escalating to `deberta-v3-base` per T-307 would have been the wrong fix — capacity isn't the problem, quantization is.

**Neither T-307 nor D-09 says which artefact the 0.75 gate applies to.** That ambiguity is what let a passing model produce a failing deployment. I resolved it as "the artefact that actually runs" and recorded that in both TASKLIST and `decisions.txt`.

## Things you should know

- **You ran 15 epochs, not 3.** I verified from `training_args.bin` that this was the only change. The result stands — best-checkpoint selection was on dev, held-out was untouched — but **the report and deck must say 15**, since TASKLIST specifies 2–3.
- **The 496 MB zip at the repo root wasn't gitignored.** `git add -A` would have committed half a gigabyte of weights. Added `*.zip`/`*.safetensors`/`*.onnx` and verified no source file got caught. You can delete `verifier-scifact.zip` now — it's unzipped to `data/models/verifier-scifact/`.
- **CONTRADICT is the weakest class** (F1 0.672) and the rarest (131 of 628). Worth one line in Limitations.
- **T-306 confirms batching makes the verifier slower** on all three models tested — 2.8–3.3× at batch=32. T-502 should feed it one pair at a time.

**Next up:** T-307 passing frees the Kaggle quota for T-332, the reranker fine-tune — but that's blocked on Phase 3B building its training triples. Phase 3B (T-320–T-326) is pure parsing, no GPU, and is the natural next block. Nothing is committed.

  arm          accuracy  macro-F1  SUPPORT  CONTRADICT   NEI

Kaggle (GPU) and local (CPU) agree to six decimals on both arms, so the table
is independently reproduced rather than copied from notebook output.

The argument for the training component is the failure mode, not the delta:
stock SUPPORT recall is 0.234 - it predicts NEI for 158 of 235 true SUPPORT
pairs. A claim filter that discards two thirds of true claims is not merely
weaker, it is unusable in the role. Fine-tuning takes that to 0.766.

T-301  scifact_pairs.py. 1463/272/628 pairs. TASKLIST's stated loading path
       does not work: scifact_entailment is script-based too, and datasets>=4
       refuses it. Reads the Hub's refs/convert/parquet branch instead. The
       train/dev split groups by claim_id - one claim spans up to five rows.
T-302  Kaggle notebook, 23 cells, every cell smoke-tested locally on CPU
       before it saw a GPU. Warm start PERMUTES the stock NLI head [1,0,2]
       rather than reinitialising it; the same permutation is what makes the
       T-305 stock arm a fair baseline. A test execs the notebook's own cells
       and asserts they match the module, verified to fail on drift.
T-304  ONNX export. fp32 is faithful (max |dlogit| 9e-6, argmax 20/20).
       SHIPS fp32, NOT int8 - see below.
T-306  25.4 claims/sec fp32 (45.7 int8); ~79 s per 2000-claim run. Batching
       makes it SLOWER on all three models tested, so T-502 must feed the
       verifier one pair at a time.

       T-332.

input.content:
"""T-320 — load the SciReviewGen mirror and record its provenance.

**Why this track exists.** ``PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.6`` names a credibility trap
that is fatal if unanswered: *"The groundedness metric is circular. The system
enforces groundedness, then measures it. Groundedness = 0.98 proves only that
the filter ran."* SciReviewGen supplies claims **humans wrote** citing papers
**humans chose**, so agreement with it is genuinely independent of our pipeline
(T-325).

**Mirror provenance — read this before citing anything.** The original dataset
is Kasanishi et al., *Findings of ACL 2023* (arXiv:2305.15186), released
**CC BY-NC 4.0**. This module reads the ungated Hugging Face mirror
``kejian/SciReviewGen``. ⚠️ **The mirrors' licence metadata is unreliable**:
``pat-jj/SciReviewGen`` declares MIT, which a mirror of S2ORC-derived data
cannot grant. **Cite Kasanishi et al. and state CC BY-NC regardless of what any
mirror card says** (T-326).

The dataset is frozen at **S2ORC 2020-07-05**, which matters twice over:
live OpenAlex retrieval surfaces post-2020 papers that are correct but score as
false positives (T-212b), and the corpus skews biomedical against our CS target
domain (T-334).

**Two columns only**, and both intended uses are recoverable by parsing::

    reference  survey_title <s> chapter <s> abstract <s> BIBnnn </s>   (repeated)
    target     the human-written chapter, with inline BIBnnn markers

Run::

    python -m researchgpt.eval.scireviewgen          # verify + record provenance
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
from typing import Any

#: The mirror actually read. Two others exist (``kdercksen/scireviewgen-csv``
#: carries the same splits and is the T-321 fallback named in the Aug 28 kill
#: switch; ``pat-jj/SciReviewGen`` mis-declares its licence).
REPO = "kejian/SciReviewGen"

#: Shard filenames are content-hashed, so they are resolved from the repo
#: listing rather than hard-coded — a re-upload would change them.
_SPLIT_PREFIX = {"train": "data/train-", "validation": "data/validation-", "test": "data/test-"}

#: Row counts from the dataset card, verified 2026-08-25. :func:`load_split`
#: checks against these: a silently re-built mirror would otherwise change the
#: evidence base without changing any code.
EXPECTED_ROWS: dict[str, int] = {"train": 84705, "validation": 4410, "test": 4457}

CITATION = (
    "Kasanishi, T., Isonuma, M., Mori, J., Sakata, I. (2023). SciReviewGen: A "
    "Large-scale Dataset for Automatic Literature Review Generation. Findings of "
    "ACL 2023. arXiv:2305.15186."
)
LICENCE = "CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial; an academic project satisfies this)"

DEFAULT_OUT = pathlib.Path("data/scireviewgen")


def shard_paths(split: str) -> list[pathlib.Path]:
    """Resolve and download the parquet shards for one split."""
    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download, list_repo_files

    prefix = _SPLIT_PREFIX[split]
    names = sorted(f for f in list_repo_files(REPO, repo_type="dataset") if f.startswith(prefix))
    if not names:
        raise SystemExit(f"no shards matching {prefix!r} in {REPO}")
    return [
        pathlib.Path(hf_hub_download(REPO, name, repo_type="dataset")) for name in names
    ]


def load_split(split: str, *, limit: int | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Read one split as a list of ``{reference, target}`` dicts.

    ``limit`` stops after that many rows, reading only as many shards as needed
    — the train split is 460 MB across three shards and most callers want a
    sample, not all 84,705 rows.
    """
    import pyarrow.parquet as pq

    rows: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    for path in shard_paths(split):
        table = pq.read_table(path)
        rows.extend(table.to_pylist())
        if limit is not None and len(rows) >= limit:
            return rows[:limit]

    expected = EXPECTED_ROWS.get(split)
    if expected is not None and len(rows) != expected:
        print(
            f"  WARNING: {split}: got {len(rows)} rows, expected {expected}. The mirror "
            f"may have been rebuilt; re-verify T-321 before trusting T-325."
        )
    return rows


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:

**Why this track exists.** ``PROJECT_PLAN.md §9.6`` names a credibility trap
that is fatal if unanswered: *"The groundedness metric is circular. The system
enforces groundedness, then measures it. Groundedness = 0.98 proves only that
the filter ran."* SciReviewGen supplies claims **humans wrote** citing papers
**humans chose**, so agreement with it is genuinely independent of our pipeline
(T-325).

**Mirror provenance — read this before citing anything.** The original dataset
is Kasanishi et al., *Findings of ACL 2023* (arXiv:2305.15186), released
**CC BY-NC 4.0**. This module reads the ungated Hugging Face mirror
``kejian/SciReviewGen``. ⚠️ **The mirrors' licence metadata is unreliable**:
``pat-jj/SciReviewGen`` declares MIT, which a mirror of S2ORC-derived data
cannot grant. **Cite Kasanishi et al. and state CC BY-NC regardless of what any
mirror card says** (T-326).

The dataset is frozen at **S2ORC 2020-07-05**, which matters twice over:
live OpenAlex retrieval surfaces post-2020 papers that are correct but score as
false positives (T-212b), and the corpus skews biomedical against our CS target
domain (T-334).

**Two columns only**, and both intended uses are recoverable by parsing::

    reference  survey_title <s> chapter <s> abstract <s> BIBnnn </s>   (repeated)
    target     the human-written chapter, with inline BIBnnn markers

"""T-321 ⛔ — parse SciReviewGen's ``reference`` column, and prove the parse is right.

``reference`` packs a repeated 4-field record into one string::

    survey_title <s> chapter_heading <s> cited_abstract <s> BIBnnn </s>

``target`` is the human-written chapter with inline ``BIBnnn`` markers pointing
into those blocks. **Everything downstream — T-322 pairs, T-324 gold sets, and
T-325, the cross-check this whole track exists for — rests on that alignment
holding.** TASKLIST flags it as the one unproven assumption in Phase 3B, because
it could only be checked against the datasets-server preview, which truncates
long cells.

**Measured here on full rows, which is the point of the task.**

The gate is the **bib-resolution rate**: of all ``BIBnnn`` markers appearing in
``target``, what fraction resolve to a block in ``reference``? TASKLIST sets
**≥ 0.95**. Below that the delimiter parse is wrong and must be fixed — *not*
worked around by silently dropping unresolved markers, which would quietly
shrink and bias the evidence base.

⚠️ **Not every citation in ``target`` is a ``BIBnnn`` marker.** Chapters also
carry plain prose citations (``(Jordan and Mitchell 2015)``) that SciReviewGen
could not link to a paper. Those are *out of scope by construction* — the gate
measures only the markers that claim to resolve, not citation coverage. Reading
it as coverage would understate the parse quality badly.

Run::

    python -m researchgpt.eval.scireviewgen_parser              # gate on validation
    python -m researchgpt.eval.scireviewgen_parser --split test --n 1000
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.eval.scireviewgen import load_split

#: The delimiters. Blocks are separated by ``</s>``; fields within a block by ``<s>``.
_BLOCK_SEP = "</s>"
_FIELD_SEP = "<s>"

#: Citation markers, in both `reference` blocks and `target` prose.
BIB_RE = re.compile(r"BIB\d+")

#: TASKLIST T-321. Below this the parse is wrong; fix it, do not drop markers.
RESOLUTION_GATE = 0.95

DEFAULT_OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/scireviewgen_parse_t321.json")


def parse_reference(reference: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Split one ``reference`` cell into ``{survey_title, chapter, bibs}``.

    ``bibs`` is ``[{bib_id, abstract}]`` in document order.

    Every block carries its own copy of the survey title and chapter heading;
    they are taken from the first block and the rest are checked for agreement
    rather than assumed (:func:`parse_stats` reports disagreements).

    Field-count robustness: a block is read as
    ``parts[0] = title, parts[1] = chapter, parts[-1] = bib_id`` with everything
    between joined back as the abstract. Measured over 6,284 validation blocks
    every block is exactly 4 fields, but an abstract containing a literal
    ``<s>`` would otherwise silently shift every field left.
    """
    blocks: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    titles: set[str] = set()
    chapters: set[str] = set()
    malformed = 0

    for raw in reference.split(_BLOCK_SEP):
        if not raw.strip():
            continue
        parts = [p.strip() for p in raw.split(_FIELD_SEP)]
        if len(parts) < 4 or not BIB_RE.fullmatch(parts[-1]):
            malformed += 1
            continue
        titles.add(parts[0])
        chapters.add(parts[1])
        blocks.append(
            {"bib_id": parts[-1], "abstract": f" {_FIELD_SEP} ".join(parts[2:-1]).strip()}
        )

    return {
        "survey_title": next(iter(titles), ""),
        "chapter": next(iter(chapters), ""),
        "bibs": blocks,
        "n_titles": len(titles),
        "n_chapters": len(chapters),
        "malformed_blocks": malformed,
    }


def target_bib_ids(target: str) -> list[str]:
    """Every ``BIBnnn`` marker in the chapter text, in order, with duplicates."""
    return BIB_RE.findall(target)


def parse_stats(rows: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run the parse over ``rows`` and compute the T-321 resolution rate."""
    markers_total = 0
    markers_resolved = 0
    rows_fully_resolved = 0
    rows_with_markers = 0
    malformed_blocks = 0
    inconsistent_header = 0
    empty_abstracts = 0
    unresolved_examples: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    bibs_per_row: list[int] = []
    markers_per_row: list[int] = []
    orphan_blocks = 0

    for row in rows:
        parsed = parse_reference(row["reference"])
        malformed_blocks += parsed["malformed_blocks"]
        if parsed["n_titles"] > 1 or parsed["n_chapters"] > 1:
            inconsistent_header += 1
        available = {b["bib_id"] for b in parsed["bibs"]}
        empty_abstracts += sum(1 for b in parsed["bibs"] if not b["abstract"])
        bibs_per_row.append(len(parsed["bibs"]))

        markers = target_bib_ids(row["target"])
        markers_per_row.append(len(markers))
        if not markers:
            continue
        rows_with_markers += 1

        resolved = [m for m in markers if m in available]
        markers_total += len(markers)
        markers_resolved += len(resolved)
        if len(resolved) == len(markers):
            rows_fully_resolved += 1
        elif len(unresolved_examples) < 5:
            unresolved_examples.append({
                "survey_title": parsed["survey_title"][:80],
                "missing": sorted(set(markers) - available)[:8],
                "available": sorted(available)[:8],
            })

        # Cited papers the chapter never actually cites in its prose.
        orphan_blocks += len(available - set(markers))

    rate = markers_resolved / markers_total if markers_total else 0.0
    return {
        "rows": len(rows),
        "rows_with_markers": rows_with_markers,
        "markers_total": markers_total,
        "markers_resolved": markers_resolved,
        "resolution_rate": rate,
        "rows_fully_resolved": rows_fully_resolved,
        "row_full_resolution_rate": rows_fully_resolved / max(rows_with_markers, 1),
        "malformed_blocks": malformed_blocks,
        "rows_with_inconsistent_header": inconsistent_header,
        "empty_abstracts": empty_abstracts,
        "orphan_blocks": orphan_blocks,
        "mean_bibs_per_row": sum(bibs_per_row) / max(len(bibs_per_row), 1),
        "mean_markers_per_row": sum(markers_per_row) / max(len(markers_per_row), 1),
        "unresolved_examples": unresolved_examples,
        "gate": RESOLUTION_GATE,
        "pass": rate >= RESOLUTION_GATE,
    }


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-321 - parse SciReviewGen and gate on it.")
    ap.add_argument("--split", default="validation", choices=["train", "validation", "test"])
    ap.add_argument("--n", type=int, default=1000,
                    help="rows to check (TASKLIST requires >= 500)")
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    print(f"T-321 - bib-resolution gate\n  split: {args.split}  rows: {args.n}\n")
    rows = load_split(args.split, limit=args.n)
    stats = parse_stats(rows)

    print(f"  rows parsed                    {stats['rows']:7,d}")
    print(f"  rows carrying BIB markers      {stats['rows_with_markers']:7,d}")
    print(f"  mean cited papers per row      {stats['mean_bibs_per_row']:7.2f}")
    print(f"  mean BIB markers per row       {stats['mean_markers_per_row']:7.2f}")
    print()
    print(f"  BIB markers in target          {stats['markers_total']:7,d}")
    print(f"  resolved to a reference block  {stats['markers_resolved']:7,d}")
    print(f"  RESOLUTION RATE                {stats['resolution_rate']:7.4f}   "
          f"gate >= {RESOLUTION_GATE}   {'PASS' if stats['pass'] else 'FAIL'}")
    print()
    print(f"  rows fully resolved            {stats['row_full_resolution_rate']:7.4f}")
    print(f"  malformed blocks               {stats['malformed_blocks']:7,d}")
    print(f"  rows w/ inconsistent header    {stats['rows_with_inconsistent_header']:7,d}")
    print(f"  empty abstracts                {stats['empty_abstracts']:7,d}")
    print(f"  cited-but-never-marked blocks  {stats['orphan_blocks']:7,d}")

    if stats["unresolved_examples"]:
        print("\n  unresolved examples:")
        for ex in stats["unresolved_examples"]:
            print(f"    {ex['survey_title']}")
            print(f"      missing {ex['missing']}  available {ex['available']}")

    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    args.out.write_text(json.dumps({"split": args.split, **stats}, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {args.out}")

    if not stats["pass"]:
        raise SystemExit(
            f"T-321 FAILED: resolution {stats['resolution_rate']:.4f} < {RESOLUTION_GATE}. "
            f"The delimiter parse is wrong - fix it. Do NOT silently drop unresolved "
            f"markers. If it still fails, fall back to kdercksen/scireviewgen-csv "
            f"before abandoning T-325 (TASKLIST Aug 28 kill switch)."
        )
    print(f"T-321 PASS: {stats['resolution_rate']:.4f} >= {RESOLUTION_GATE}. "
          f"T-322..T-325 are unblocked.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
